lem-cover-exact-comparison-artin-tits-no.title: Intermediate exact sequences and deck morphism in Theorem 6.7

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection, and $W_J,A_J$ the standard parabolic subgroups generated by $J$. Put $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, $\mathcal R$ the reduced ribbon groupoid, $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ the crossing-to-ribbon functor and $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ the orbit functor. A vertex group is the group of arrows from a specified object to itself. Write $d=(e,J)$, $\mathcal D_J=\mathcal D_d$ and $\mathcal R_J$ for the vertex group of $\mathcal R$ at $J$.

Let $X$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement, $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$ the equivariant equivalence, $x=p(d)$ and $\bar x$ the image of $x$ in $X/N$. With first-path-first products and ordinary composition of deck transformations, the exact sequence $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal Q}(\mathcal D/N)_{\mathcal Qd}\to N\to1$ is isomorphic, with identity on $N$, to the topological covering sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)\to N\to1$. It is also isomorphic, with identity on $\mathcal D_J$ and $N$, to $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal G}\mathcal R_J\xrightarrow{\psi}N\to1$.

For $\mu\in\mathcal R_J$, its unique $\mathcal G$-lift from $d$ ends at $(\pi(\mu),J)$; in particular $\pi(\mu)$ is the minimum-length representative of its right $W_J$-coset and $\psi(\mu)=\pi(\mu)W_J$. Under the isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$ induced by quotienting by $A_J$, $\psi$ agrees with the map $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N$ induced by $\pi$.

More explicitly, let $q_J:\mathcal R_J\to N(A,J)$ be the quotient isomorphism, let $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ be the isomorphism with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\mathcal Q$, and let $\bar p:\mathcal D/N\to\Pi_1(X/N)$ be induced by $p$. Write $p_d$, $\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}$ and $\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd}$ for the induced vertex-group maps. The comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the topological sequence has components $(p_d,\bar p_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$; the comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the ribbon sequence has components $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_J},\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$. Consequently the resulting algebraic-to-topological comparison has middle map $\Phi=\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}\circ(\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd})^{-1}\circ q_J^{-1}:N(A,J)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and $\mathcal D(J)$ its groupoid completion. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid and $\mathcal G:\mathcal D(J)\to\mathcal R(J)$ the functor sending a chamber label $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple crossing with index $a\notin I$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$.

The functor $\mathcal G$ is a groupoid covering: for every chamber $C$ and every arrow of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $\mathcal G(C)$, there is exactly one arrow of $\mathcal D(J)$ with source $C$ and that image. Each elementary ribbon lifts from $(x,I)$ to the corresponding simple wall crossing. The two sides of each defining ribbon-lcm relation lift from a fixed source chamber to equal morphisms of $\mathcal D^+(J)$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, so its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, and fix a subset $J$ of its vertices. Use the chamber labels $(x,I)$, positive arrangement category $\mathcal D^+(J)$, its groupoid completion $\mathcal D(J)$, and reduced ribbon groupoid $\mathcal R(J)$ of the indicated definitions. A geodesic is a chamber path of minimum crossing length among paths with the same endpoints. For $w\in W$, write $\sigma_w$ for its positive reduced-word lift in the Artin group.

The assignment $\mathcal G(x,I)=I$ and $\mathcal G(\omega_{a,I})=\mu_{a,I}$ extends to a well-defined functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D(J)\to\mathcal R(J)$. If a geodesic travels through labels $(x_1,I_1),\ldots,(x_n,I_n)$, with crossing indices $a_i$, its image is the arrow $I_1\to I_n$ labelled by $\sigma_{x_1^{-1}x_n}=\mu_{a_1,I_1}\cdots\mu_{a_{n-1},I_{n-1}}$. In particular its image depends only on its endpoints, including when the path is empty.

lem-equivariant-topological-equivalence-.title: Equivariant equivalence with fundamental groupoids

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Put $G=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, where $W_J$ is generated by $J$. Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ be the groupoid completion of the positive relative chamber category. Thus its objects are chambers and its generating arrows are directed crossings of adjacent chambers, subject to equality of positive geodesic galleries with the same endpoints and formal inversion of arrows.

The space $X$ is nonempty, path-connected and locally path-connected.

There is a $G$-equivariant equivalence $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$, where $\Pi_1(X)$ has points of $X$ as objects and endpoint-fixed path-homotopy classes as arrows. Equivariance means $p(gC)=g p(C)$ on objects and $p(g\alpha)=g p(\alpha)$ on arrows. With $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/G$ the orbit functor and $q:X\to X/G$ the topological orbit map, $p$ induces an equivalence $\bar p:\mathcal D/G\to\Pi_1(X/G)$ satisfying $\bar p\,Q=q_*p$. The map $q$ is a normal covering. An equivalence means a functor equipped with a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms to the two identity functors; the Axiom of Choice is used below to choose connecting paths for all objects.

lem-finite-parabolic-wall-formula-artin-.title: Simplified wall crossing for a finite parabolic

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system indexed by the vertices $\Gamma_0$ of its Coxeter diagram, let $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$, and let $(x,I)$ be a chamber label: $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Choose $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$ and put $K=I\cup\{a\}$. Suppose $W_K$ is finite. For a finite parabolic $W_L$, write $w_L$ for its longest element and $\iota_L$ for its opposition permutation, characterized by $w_L\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_L(i)}$ for $i\in L$.

With the simple wall-crossing element $v_{a,I}$ and pair $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)$ defined in [def-simple-wall-crossing-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-simple-wall-crossing-artin-tits-normalisers), one has $v_{a,I}=w_Iw_K$ and $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)=(xw_Iw_K,K\setminus\{\iota_K(a)\})$.

lem-finite-separation-artin-tits-normali.title: Only finitely many hyperplanes separate two Tits-cone points

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, with geometric roots $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup\Phi^-$ in the real vector space with simple-root basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in\Gamma_0}$, and let $\Theta$ be its algebraic dual with the contragredient action. Put $\overline C=\{h\in\Theta:h(\alpha_i)\geq0\text{ for every }i\in\Gamma_0\}$ and $\mathrm{Cone}=\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C$. For $\alpha\in\Phi$ put $H_\alpha=\{h\in\Theta:h(\alpha)=0\}$ and $\mathcal H=\{H_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}$. Say that $H_\alpha$ separates $f,g\in\mathrm{Cone}$ when $f(\alpha)$ and $g(\alpha)$ have opposite strict signs.

For $f,g\in\mathrm{Cone}$, only finitely many hyperplanes in $\mathcal H$ separate $f$ and $g$. The generating set may be infinite; in finite rank these conventions agree with the stated Tits-cone and separation definitions.

lem-finite-wall-path-artin-tits-normalis.title: Finite wall-crossing connectivity

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$ be the intersection of the Tits cone with $\Theta_J=\{f:f(\alpha_j)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\}$, and let $\mathcal H^J$ be the distinct proper traces on $\Theta_J$ of root hyperplanes. Chambers are the connected components of the relative arrangement complement; distinct chambers are adjacent when their closures share a wall, a codimension-one intersection with an arrangement hyperplane.

Write $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ for the pairs $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ of minimum length in $xW_I$. For $a\notin I$, let $D=[I,a]$ be the component containing $a$ in the Coxeter diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$. When $W_D$ is finite, the simple wall crossing is $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)=(xw_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D,(I\cup\{a\})\setminus\{\iota_D(a)\})$, where $w_L$ is the longest element of the finite parabolic $W_L$ and $w_D\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_D(i)}$.

Any two chambers are related by a finite sequence of simple wall crossings. In particular, this follows from local finiteness of the relative-interior arrangement and the identification of its chambers and adjacency relation with those of the full relative arrangement. The empty sequence is allowed when the two chambers coincide.

Let $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$ be the intersection of the Tits cone with $\Theta_J=\{f:f(\alpha_j)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\}$, and let $\mathcal H^J$ be the distinct proper traces on $\Theta_J$ of root hyperplanes. Chambers are the connected components of the relative arrangement complement; distinct chambers are adjacent when their closures share a wall, a codimension-one intersection with an arrangement hyperplane.

Write $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ for the pairs $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ of minimum length in $xW_I$. For $a\notin I$, let $D=[I,a]$ be the component containing $a$ in the Coxeter diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$. When $W_D$ is finite, the simple wall crossing is $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)=(xw_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D,(I\cup\{a\})\setminus\{\iota_D(a)\})$, where $w_L$ is the longest element of the finite parabolic $W_L$ and $w_D\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_D(i)}$.

Any two chambers are related by a finite sequence of simple wall crossings. In particular, this follows from local finiteness of the relative-interior arrangement and the identification of its chambers and adjacency relation with those of the full relative arrangement. The empty sequence is allowed when the two chambers coincide.

lem-nonnegative-inverse-interface-artin-.title: Nonnegative inverse matrices preserve extremal basis rays

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $A$ be an invertible $n\times n$ real matrix such that $A$ and $A^{-1}$ are entrywise nonnegative. Then $A=PD$, where $P$ is a permutation matrix and $D$ is a diagonal matrix with strictly positive diagonal entries. Here a permutation matrix has exactly one entry $1$ in each row and each column and all other entries zero.

Suppose in addition that $A$ is the change-of-basis matrix from an ordered basis $\mathcal B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ to an ordered basis $\mathcal C=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ of the canonical Coxeter representation, and that all these basis vectors are roots. Then $D=I_n$, so $A$ is a permutation matrix. The case $n=0$ is allowed.

lem-nonnegative-root-bases-artin-tits-no.title: Root bases and nonnegative matrices for chamber labels

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, canonical geometric representation $V=\bigoplus_{i\in\Gamma_0}\mathbb R\alpha_i$, and positive roots $\Phi^+$. For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, put $V_I=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}$ and let $\Phi_I^+$ be the positive roots of the standard parabolic subgroup $W_I$. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and $(y,K)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$; explicitly, $W_Jy=yW_K$ and $y$ has minimum length in $yW_K$.

Then $y^{-1}\alpha_j\in\Phi_K^+$ for every $j\in J$, and $y\alpha_k\in\Phi_J^+$ for every $k\in K$. The maps $y:V_K\to V_J$ and $y^{-1}:V_J\to V_K$ are inverse isomorphisms. Their matrices in the indicated simple-root bases are entrywise nonnegative and are permutation matrices. Consequently $y\{\alpha_k:k\in K\}=\{\alpha_j:j\in J\}$. The assertions include empty $J$ and $K$; neither $W$ nor the parabolic subgroups are assumed finite.

lem-normaliser-chamber-action-artin-tits.title: Normaliser action on labels, orbits and adjacency

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$ and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $W_I$ for the standard parabolic subgroup generated by the simple reflections indexed by $I$, and let $\ell$ be Coxeter length. The chamber-label set $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ consists of the pairs $(x,I)$ such that $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ for the normaliser quotient.

Under the chamber bijection $(x,I)\mapsto xC_I$, the quotient action on the relative cone induces an action on $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$. For $\bar g\in N(W,J)$ and any representative $g\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$, it is given by $\bar g\cdot(x,I)=(y,I)$, where $y$ is the unique minimum-length element of $gxW_I$. Any two labels with the same second component lie in the same orbit, and the action is free: a quotient element fixing a label is the identity.

If $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)=(xv_{a,I},K)$ is a simple wall crossing to an adjacent chamber, then $\omega_{a,I}(\bar g\cdot(x,I))=\bar g\cdot\omega_{a,I}(x,I)$. Thus the action preserves adjacency and the crossing index $a$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, $A$ its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection and $P=\ker\pi$. For a subset $J\subseteq S$, let $W_J$ and $A_J$ be the standard parabolic subgroups. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$, and let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$. Then $\pi$ induces $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N(W,J)$ and the sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\xrightarrow{\overline\pi}N(W,J)\to1$ is exact. Here exactness means that the inclusion $N(P,J)\hookrightarrow N(A,J)$ is injective, its image equals $\ker\overline\pi$, and $\overline\pi$ is surjective.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and let $V$ be its canonical real representation with simple-root basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in\Gamma_0}$ and dual space $\Theta=V^*$, equipped with the contragredient action. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Write $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle$, $\Theta_J=\{f\in\Theta:f(\alpha_j)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\}$, and $C_L=\{f\in\Theta_L:f(\alpha_i)>0\text{ for all }i\notin L\}$ for $L\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Let $\mathrm{Cone}$ be the union of the $W$-translates of the closed fundamental chamber, and put $\mathrm{Cone}(J)=\mathrm{Cone}\cap\Theta_J$.

The normaliser $\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)=\{g\in W:gW_Jg^{-1}=W_J\}$ preserves $\Theta_J$, and the kernel of its action on $\Theta_J$ is exactly $W_J$. Consequently its quotient $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ acts faithfully by linear maps on $\Theta_J$. This action preserves $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$ and its stratification into the translates $xC_L\subseteq\Theta_J$: for every such stratum and every lift $g\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$ of $\bar g\in N(W,J)$, one has $\bar g\,(xC_L)=(gx)C_L$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, Coxeter group $W$, length $\ell$, simple generators $s_i$, and simple roots $\alpha_i$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group with standard generators $\sigma_i$ and positive submonoid $A^+$ generated by them. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and a chamber label $(x,I)$, meaning $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Choose $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, put $T=I\cup\{a\}$, and put $K=T\setminus\{\iota_T(a)\}$. Here $W_L$ is the subgroup generated by $\{s_i:i\in L\}$, $w_L$ is its longest element, and $\iota_L$ is its opposition permutation, defined by $w_L\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_L(i)}$.

Let $v_{a,I}$ be the simple wall-crossing element and $\mu_{a,I}$ the positive elementary ribbon element. Then $\mu_{a,I}$ is the positive reduced-word lift of $v_{a,I}$ and belongs to $A^+$. Moreover $K$ is an associate of $J$, meaning $W_K$ is conjugate to $W_J$, and $\mu_{a,I}$ is a morphism $I\to K$ in the ribbon groupoid $\mathcal R'(J)$: explicitly, $A_I^+\mu_{a,I}=\mu_{a,I}A_K^+$, where $A_L^+$ is the submonoid of $A$ generated by $\{\sigma_i:i\in L\}$.

lem-ribbon-lcm-lift-artin-tits-normalise.title: Ribbon lcms lift two-generator Brink–Howlett elements

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and let $A$ be its Artin group with positive submonoid $A^+$ and natural homomorphism $\pi:A\to W$. Fix $J\subseteq S$ and an associate $I$ of $J$, meaning that $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$. For $a\in S\setminus I$, let $\mu_{a,I}$ be the elementary ribbon and $v_{a,I}$ its corresponding elementary Brink–Howlett morphism, with the conventions of [def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers) and [def-standard-expressions-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-standard-expressions-artin-tits-normalisers). A positive lift $\sigma_w$ of $w\in W$ is the Artin word obtained from a reduced Coxeter word for $w$.

For distinct $a,b\in S\setminus I$, let $q=v_{a,b,I}$ be the two-generator morphism of [lem-two-generator-minimal-artin-tits-normalisers](item-lem-two-generator-minimal-artin-tits-normalisers), and let $L=\mu_{a,I}\vee\mu_{b,I}$ be the least common multiple for left divisibility in $A^+$. Its two elementary-ribbon expressions, beginning respectively with $\mu_{a,I}$ and $\mu_{b,I}$, are precisely the factorwise positive lifts of the two standard expressions of $q$. Let $m$ and $n$ be the respective numbers of elementary factors in these two ribbon expressions. Then $m=n$, and $\pi(L)=q$. Moreover $q$ is the join of $v_{a,I}$ and $v_{b,I}$ in the prefix weak order: $u\leq v$ means $v=ux$ with $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+\ell(x)$. This is the order called weak left Bruhat order in the article.

For $a=b$, the lcm is $\mu_{a,I}$ and the join is $v_{a,I}$; the assertion of two distinct expressions is not made in this case.

lem-segment-intersections-artin-tits-nor.title: Segment intersections and the inversion bound

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with its real reflection representation on $V$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$, dual space $\Theta$, contragredient action, closed fundamental chamber $\overline C$, Tits cone $\mathrm{Cone}=\bigcup_{u\in W}u\overline C$, and set $\mathcal H=\{H_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}$ of distinct root hyperplanes, where $H_\alpha=\{x\in\Theta:x(\alpha)=0\}$. Write $\ell(w)$ for Coxeter word length. For $f,g\in\mathrm{Cone}$ put $[f,g]=\{(1-t)f+tg:0\leq t\leq1\}$ and $(f,g)=[f,g]\setminus\{f,g\}$. A hyperplane separates $f$ and $g$ when the values of a defining linear functional at them have opposite strict signs.

A hyperplane $H\in\mathcal H$ separates $f$ and $g$ if and only if $H\cap(f,g)$ consists of one point and $H$ does not contain $[f,g]$. If $f\in\overline C$, $g\in w\overline C$ and $h\in(f,g)$, then $|\{H_\alpha\in\mathcal H:H_\alpha\cap(f,g)=\{h\}\}|\leq\ell(w^{-1})$. For arbitrary $f,g\in\mathrm{Cone}$, the set $\{h\in(f,g):H\cap[f,g]=\{h\}\text{ for some }H\in\mathcal H\}$ is finite.

lem-standard-geodesic-artin-tits-normali.title: Standard expressions correspond to geodesics

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. In the associated relative arrangement, chambers have labels $(x,I)$; a chamber path is a finite nonempty sequence of labels with consecutive chambers adjacent, and is geodesic if its number of crossings is minimal among paths with the same endpoints. The Brink–Howlett groupoid $\mathcal{BH}(J)$ has associates of $J$ as objects, and its morphisms are the elements carrying the target's simple-root set onto the source's simple-root set. Labels of composable morphisms multiply from left to right.

For $a\notin I$, let $D=[I,a]$ be the component containing $a$ in the diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$, and suppose $W_D$ is finite. Write $w_L$ for the longest element of a finite standard parabolic $W_L$, put $v_{a,I}=w_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D$ for the simple wall-crossing element, and write $\omega_{a,I}$ for the corresponding crossing. A standard expression is a composable sequence of such elements whose Coxeter lengths sum to the length of their product.

Given a nonempty finite sequence of specified simple crossings, their concatenation is a well-defined geodesic path exactly when each target chamber equals the next source chamber and their elements form a standard expression with the same initial object. Every standard expression beginning at $I$ lifts, from any chamber $(x,I)$, to a unique geodesic crossing path. If its product is $w:I\to K$, this lift ends at $(xw,K)$. Every morphism $w:I\to K$ has a standard expression. The identity is represented by the empty expression and the corresponding one-chamber path.

lem-translate-path-artin-tits-normaliser.title: Translation between relative arrangements in the geodesic argument

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Work with the finite-rank real Coxeter representation and relative arrangements, with arbitrary Coxeter type and $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Let $(z,L)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$. Then $z^{-1}$ maps the relative arrangement for $J$ bijectively to that for $L$, including their cone interiors and distinct relative hyperplanes. It induces a bijection of chamber labels sending $(z,L)$ to $(e,L)$: the image of $(x,I)$ is $(x',I)$, where $x'$ is the unique minimum-length element of $z^{-1}xW_I$.

Under this bijection every chamber path $p$ maps to a path of the same length; geodesicity is preserved and reflected. Each simple wall crossing retains its index $a$ and element $v_{a,I}$, so the wall word element satisfies $v_{z^{-1}p}=v_p$.

lem-two-generator-minimal-artin-tits-nor.title: Two-generator minimal common left multiple

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $I$ be an associate of $J$ and let distinct $a,b\in I^c$ satisfy $|\Phi_{I+a+b}\setminus\Phi_I|<\infty$. There exist an associate $K$ and $v_{a,b,I}\in\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{BH}}(I,K)$ such that $v_{a,I},v_{b,I}$ are left divisors of $v_{a,b,I}$ in $W$. It has exactly two standard expressions, of the same length, one starting with $v_{a,I}$ and one with $v_{b,I}$. Any Brink–Howlett morphism from $I$ left-divisible by both $v_{a,I},v_{b,I}$ is left-divisible by $v_{a,b,I}$. Thus $v_{a,b,I}$ is minimal both for left divisibility and for standard-expression length among such morphisms.

More explicitly, put $T=I\cup\{a,b\}$, and let $D$ be the union of the connected components of the diagram induced on $T$ that meet $\{a,b\}$. Then $W_D$ is finite, and we choose the morphism above to be $v_{a,b,I}=(w_Dw_{D\cap I})^{-1}$, with $K$ the associate target supplied by the finite-relative-longest construction. Here $w_L$ denotes the longest element of the finite parabolic subgroup $W_L$.

lem-two-geodesics-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Two-geodesic wall-crossing lemma

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with diagram vertex set $\Gamma_0$, geometric root set $\Phi$, and Coxeter length $\ell$. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. For $L\subseteq\Gamma_0$, let $W_L$ be the subgroup generated by its simple reflections and $\Phi_L=\{w\alpha_i:w\in W_L,\ i\in L\}$. An associate of $J$ is a subset whose standard parabolic subgroup is conjugate to $W_J$. The Brink–Howlett groupoid $\mathcal{BH}(J)$ has these associates as objects; its morphisms $I\to K$ are the elements $w\in W$ satisfying $\{w\alpha_k:k\in K\}=\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}$, with composition by multiplication from left to right.

In the relative arrangement $(\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$, write $(x,I)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ for a chamber label. A chamber path is a finite sequence of adjacent chambers; it is geodesic if its number of crossings is minimal among paths with the same endpoints. For $a\notin I$, when the component $D=[I,a]$ containing $a$ in the diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$ has finite $W_D$, put $v_{a,I}=w_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D$, where $w_L$ is the longest element of the finite parabolic $W_L$. Write $\omega_{a,I}$ for the associated simple wall crossing. A standard expression is a composable sequence of these wall-crossing elements whose Coxeter lengths sum to the length of their product.

Let distinct $a,b\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$ satisfy $|\Phi_{I\cup\{a,b\}}\setminus\Phi_I|<\infty$, and let $(x,I)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$. Let $q=v_{a,b,I}:I\to K$ be the two-generator element supplied by [lem-two-generator-minimal-artin-tits-normalisers](item-lem-two-generator-minimal-artin-tits-normalisers). Its two standard expressions lift to exactly two geodesic paths of equal length from $(x,I)$ to $(xq,K)$, beginning respectively with $\omega_{a,I}$ and $\omega_{b,I}$. If a chamber $C$ admits geodesics from $(x,I)$ beginning with each of these crossings, then some geodesic from $(x,I)$ to $C$ passes through $(xq,K)$.

lem-wall-is-morphism-artin-tits-normalis.title: Wall-crossing elements are Brink–Howlett morphisms

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with simple generators $s_i$ and simple roots $\alpha_i$ indexed by the vertices $\Gamma_0$ of its Coxeter diagram. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$, and let $I$ be an associate of $J$, meaning that $W_I=\langle s_i:i\in I\rangle$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$. Choose $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, and let $D=[I,a]$ be the component containing $a$ in the diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$. Suppose $W_D$ is finite. For a finite standard parabolic $W_L$, write $w_L$ for its longest element and $\iota_L$ for the permutation of $L$ such that $w_L\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_L(i)}$. Put $E=D\setminus\{a\}$, $K=(I\cup\{a\})\setminus\{\iota_D(a)\}$ and $v_{a,I}=w_Ew_D$.

Then $K$ is an associate of $J$, and $v_{a,I}$ is a Brink–Howlett morphism from $I$ to $K$: explicitly, $\{v_{a,I}\alpha_k:k\in K\}=\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}$.

lem-wall-length-halfspace-artin-tits-nor.title: Length additivity and the base-chamber half-space

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with simple generators $s_i$ and simple roots $\alpha_i$ indexed by $\Gamma_0$. Use its standard geometric representation, root signs, word length $\ell$, dual space $\Theta$, and contragredient action. For $L\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $W_L=\langle s_i:i\in L\rangle$. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and a label $(x,I)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$, so $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. The label represents the relative chamber $xC_I$, where $C_I$ consists of dual vectors vanishing on $\alpha_i$ for $i\in I$ and positive on the other simple roots.

Choose $a\notin I$, let $D=[I,a]$ be the component containing $a$ of the diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$, and suppose $W_D$ is finite. Put $v_{a,I}=w_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D$, using the longest elements of the indicated finite parabolics. Suppose the pair $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)$ is a label adjacent to $(x,I)$. Then $\ell(xv_{a,I})=\ell(x)+\ell(v_{a,I})$ if and only if the base chamber $C_J$ and $xC_I$ lie in the same open half-space of $H_{x\alpha_a}=\{f\in\Theta:f(x\alpha_a)=0\}$.

op-classical-kpi-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Classical K(pi,1) conjecture

statement.heading: Open problem
statement.source_excerpt:
In the finite-rank geometric convention, let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite; $W$ need not be finite. Let $\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}$ be its classical complexified complement, put $Y=\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}/W$, choose $Z\in\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}$, and let $\overline Z\in Y$ be its orbit. Use the Artin–Tits group $A=\pi_1(Y,\overline Z)$ with its supplied identification with the presented Artin group. Is $Y$ aspherical, meaning $\pi_n(Y,\overline Z)=0$ for every $n\geq2$?

Equivalently, does this specified quotient $Y$ have the homotopy type of a $K(A,1)$, with the fundamental-group identification transported to the CW model? This is the article's classifying-space question in the usual homotopy-type sense. The question concerns $Y$ itself; the existence of some unrelated $K(A,1)$ does not answer it.

op-normaliser-kpi-artin-tits-normalisers.title: K(pi,1) conjecture for arbitrary normaliser quotients

statement.heading: Open problem
statement.source_excerpt:
The authors' Conjecture 1.10 is: “Theorem 1.8 holds for any Coxeter group $W$.” We retain that wording as the attributed question.

For its precise formulation in the finite-rank geometric convention of *Reflecting hyperplanes, fundamental chamber and Tits cone*, let $(W,S)$ be any Coxeter system with finite $S$, let $J\subseteq S$, and allow $W$ to be infinite. Use the groups $N(W,J)$, $N(A,J)$ and $N(P,J)$ of *Normalisers and their quotients*, and put $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ for the relative complexified complement of *Relative complexified hyperplane complement*. Choose $x\in X$ and let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$.

The algebraic sequence of *Normaliser quotient exact sequence* and the geometric covering sequence of *Relative free action, normal cover and exact sequence* are

$$1\longrightarrow N(P,J)\longrightarrow N(A,J)\longrightarrow N(W,J)\longrightarrow1$$

and

$$1\longrightarrow\pi_1(X,x)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\longrightarrow N(W,J)\longrightarrow1.$$

prop-adjacent-wall-formula-artin-tits-no.title: Adjacent chambers and inverse wall-crossing elements

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Work in the finite-rank canonical real Coxeter representation and its dual relative chamber arrangement, with arbitrary Coxeter type and arbitrary $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Let $(x,I),(y,K)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ label adjacent chambers $xC_I,yC_K\subseteq\Theta_J$ with common closed wall $F$. There are unique $a\in I^c$, $a'\in K^c$ describing this wall, that is, $F=\overline{xC_{I+a}}=\overline{yC_{K+a'}}$, where closures are taken in $\Theta_J$. These indices satisfy $I+a=K+a'$, the parabolic subgroups $W_{[I,a]}=W_{[K,a']}$ are finite, and $\omega_{a,I}(x,I)=(y,K)$, $\omega_{a',K}(y,K)=(x,I)$. In particular $v_{a,I}v_{a',K}=v_{a',K}v_{a,I}=e$. Here $I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$ and $I+a=I\cup\{a\}$. Neither $W_I$ nor $W_{I+a}$ is assumed finite.

prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-chamber-flop-nc.title: Chambers label smooth minimal models and their NCCR categories

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Use the complete-local isolated complex cDV smooth flopping setting and the finite arrangement $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ of the cited local interfaces. Let $\operatorname{CM}R$ consist of the zero module and the finite $R$-modules of depth three, with $R$-linear maps. Write $\operatorname{add}M$ for summands of finite direct sums of $M$. A generator has $R\in\operatorname{add}M$; basic means a finite sum of pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposable modules. A cluster-tilting object $M\in\operatorname{CM}R$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{add}M=\{L\in\operatorname{CM}R:\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(L,M)=0\}=\{L\in\operatorname{CM}R:\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,L)=0\}.$$
For a basic cluster-tilting generator $M=M_i\oplus\widehat M$ with $M_i$ nonfree indecomposable, its mutation $\nu_iM=M_i'\oplus\widehat M$ replaces $M_i$ by the unique other indecomposable complement, up to isomorphism, that leaves the module cluster-tilting.

Every chamber $C$ labels a minimal model $f_C:X_C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and a basic cluster-tilting generator $M_C$, with NCCR $\Lambda_C=\operatorname{End}_R M_C$. All these models are nonsingular projective crepant resolutions. Choose the compatible basic globally generated Van den Bergh vector bundles $V_C$ (finite locally free sheaves) in the convention of Hirano–Wemyss Setup 4.1, using the setting's fixed $\mathcal V$ at the initial chamber, with $H^0(X_C,V_C)=M_C$ and $\operatorname{End}_{X_C}V_C\cong\Lambda_C$. Their tilting equivalences are
$$E_C:=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X_C}(V_C,-):D^b(\operatorname{coh}X_C)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b(\operatorname{mod}\Lambda_C).$$
Use bounded derived categories, finite right modules and exact functors with the conventions of the cited definitions. Here $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}$ is total right-derived Hom; the existence of these bundles and equivalences is imported.

For an oriented adjacent pair $C\to D$, a single exceptional curve flops and $M_D\cong\nu_iM_C$ at its corresponding nonfree summand. Fix this isomorphism and the induced endomorphism-ring identifications. Put $T_{CD}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_C,M_D)$, a left $\Lambda_D$, right $\Lambda_C$ bimodule via postcomposition and precomposition. The mutation equivalence is
$$t_{CD}:=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda_C}(T_{CD},-):D^b(\operatorname{mod}\Lambda_C)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b(\operatorname{mod}\Lambda_D).$$

Let $X_C\to Y_i\leftarrow X_D$ be the common contraction of that curve and its flop. For the ordinary fibre product $Z_i=X_C\times_{Y_i}X_D$, write $p_C:Z_i\to X_C$ and $p_D:Z_i\to X_D$ for the projections. Choose the Bridgeland–Chen functor in the direction
$$B_{DC}:=\mathbf R(p_C)_*\mathbf Lp_D^*:D^b(\operatorname{coh}X_D)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b(\operatorname{coh}X_C).$$
This is the Fourier–Mukai functor with structure-sheaf kernel $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$; $\mathbf Lp_D^*$ and $\mathbf R(p_C)_*$ denote derived pullback and pushforward. With the compatible choices above, the precise comparison is the natural isomorphism
$$t_{CD}\circ E_C\cong E_D\circ B_{DC}^{-1}:D^b(\operatorname{coh}X_C)\longrightarrow D^b(\operatorname{mod}\Lambda_D).$$
The inverse denotes a quasi-inverse equivalence. In particular, after transport, $E_D^{-1}\circ t_{CD}\circ E_C\cong B_{DC}^{-1}$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Use the complete-local isolated-cDV smooth setting of [def-author-5f10a31d9e26-complete-local-flop-setting](item-def-author-5f10a31d9e26-complete-local-flop-setting), the finite simplicial arrangement of [prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-slice-restriction-contract](item-prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-slice-restriction-contract), and the categories of [prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-chamber-flop-nccr-dictionary](item-prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-chamber-flop-nccr-dictionary). Positive paths of minimum edge length are geodesics as in [def-geodesic-path-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-geodesic-path-artin-tits-normalisers). Any two such paths with the same endpoints induce naturally isomorphic compositions of the geometric flop functors. Here naturally isomorphic is used in the sense of [math:def-natural-isomorphism](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-natural-isomorphism).

The Deligne groupoid is generated by directed simple wall crossings, with relations identifying all positive minimum paths with the same endpoints, and formal inverses adjoined. Write $\mathcal G$ for this groupoid and $U=\mathbb C^n\setminus\mathcal H_{\Lambda,\mathbb C}$ for the complexified arrangement complement. For a chamber $C$, choose a basepoint $x_C\in C\subset U$ and fix a group isomorphism $\iota_C:\pi_1(U,x_C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal G}(C,C)$ furnished by the cited vertex-group theorem. Here the fundamental group consists of based loop classes with the multiplication convention of [math:def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group](https://alphabetamath.cc/item/def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group); $\iota_C$ is chosen as a group isomorphism for this convention, not asserted to be a literal equality or a canonical identification.

The flop and mutation equivalences give a groupoid representation in exact equivalences modulo natural isomorphism. If $F_C$ denotes its restriction to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal G}(C,C)$, the induced action of the based fundamental group on the corresponding derived category is $\rho_C=F_C\circ\iota_C$. For the smooth complete-local setting this action is faithful.

source_references.statement: Minimum flop chains between crepant resolutions of isolated cDV singularities give naturally isomorphic composites. A finite simplicial arrangement Deligne vertex group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of its complexified complement. A faithful groupoid functor induces an injective homomorphism from this fundamental group by transporting its vertex-group restriction through that isomorphism. In the complete-local smooth flop setting the mutation representation and induced action are faithful.
source_references.hypotheses: Algebraically closed characteristic-zero base; complete-local smooth threefold flopping contraction for faithfulness, and crepant resolutions of isolated cDV R for the geometric minimum-chain assertion; finite simplicial arrangement for the groupoid-topology assertion.

Theorem 2.8 states an isomorphism without specifying a basepoint or a particular isomorphism; the item makes those choices explicit, without claiming a canonical identification. The Deligne, torsion-pair and faithfulness proofs are imported, not reconstructed; no arbitrary-type or singular-source extension is imported.

prop-author-5f10a31d9e26-slice-restricti.title: Generic slicing identifies flop stability walls with restricted ADE walls

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Use the complete-local smooth flop, the basic globally generated bundle $\mathcal V$, its algebra $\Lambda=\operatorname{End}_R H^0(X,\mathcal V)$ and rank vector $r=(1,(r_i)_{i\in I})$ fixed in the setting definition, with $I=\Delta\setminus J$. Let $\Phi_\Delta\subset E$ be the finite reduced crystallographic ADE root system with simple-root basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in\Delta}$ labelled by the same vertices as the exceptional curves $E_i$ of the minimal surface resolution. Normalize $(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)=2$, with $(\alpha_i,\alpha_k)=-1$ for adjacent distinct vertices and $0$ for nonadjacent distinct vertices. Identify $\mathbb R^\Delta$ with $E^*$ by the evaluation coordinates $\vartheta_i=\vartheta(\alpha_i)$. The real stability space $\Theta_r(\Lambda)$, for right modules of this dimension vector and the stated submodule inequality, identifies by the surviving-curve coordinates with
$$L=\{\vartheta\in\mathbb R^{\Delta}:\vartheta_j=0\ (j\in J)\},\qquad\vartheta_i=\theta_i\ (i\in I).$$
Its chamber walls are exactly the distinct proper intersections $L\cap\alpha^\perp$ for roots $\alpha\in\Phi_\Delta$ with $L\not\subseteq\alpha^\perp$. Here, in simple-root dual coordinates, $\alpha=\sum_i c_i\alpha_i$ has $\alpha^\perp=\{\vartheta:\sum_i c_i\vartheta_i=0\}$. This finite simplicial arrangement is the geometric arrangement $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ used for flop and mutation functors. It is an intersection arrangement, not in general a Coxeter arrangement.

In addition, the common base $R$ is isomorphic as a complete-local $\mathbb C$-algebra to $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak n}}$ for some finitely generated $\mathbb C$-algebra $B$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$.

prop-chamber-open-set-properties-artin-t.title: Contractibility and intersection components of chamber open sets

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Use the relative real space $E$, its finite hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal H^J$, its complexified complement, and the chamber sets $X_C$, $X_{C,C'}$ and $X_{C',C}$ of the chamber-set definition. A chamber is a connected component of the real arrangement complement; adjacent chambers share a wall. Then $X_C$ is open and contractible. If $C$ and $C'$ are adjacent, $X_C\cap X_{C'}$ has exactly two connected components, namely $X_{C,C'}$ and $X_{C',C}$.

prop-chambers-morphisms-artin-tits-norma.title: Correspondence between chamber labels and Brink–Howlett morphisms

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, with vertices $\Gamma_0$, simple roots $\alpha_i$, length $\ell$, and standard parabolic subgroups $W_I=\langle s_i:i\in I\rangle$. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. A subset $I$ is an associate of $J$ when $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$. The chamber-label set $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ consists of pairs $(x,I)$ such that $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. The Brink–Howlett morphisms $I\to K$ are the elements $w\in W$ satisfying $w\{\alpha_k:k\in K\}=\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}$. The universal wall groupoid has these labels as objects and exactly one arrow from $(x,I)$ to $(y,K)$, labelled $x^{-1}y$.

For associates $I,K$ of $J$, if $(x,I),(y,K)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$, then $x^{-1}y\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{BH}(J)}(I,K)$. Conversely, if $w\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{BH}(J)}(I,K)$ and $(x,I)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$, then $(xw,K)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$, and $w$ labels the unique arrow from $(x,I)$ to $(xw,K)$ in $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$. Under the relative-chamber labelling bijection, the same assertions apply to the corresponding geometric chambers.

prop-classical-cover-artin-tits-normalis.title: Classical free action and covering exact sequence

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite. Let $\Theta$ be the dual of its canonical real reflection representation, with the contragredient action, Tits cone $\mathrm{Cone}$, and set $\mathcal H$ of distinct root hyperplanes. Put $\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}=(\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ}\times\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ})\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}(H\times H)$, with its subspace topology and the diagonal $W$-action. For any $Z\in\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}$, write $\overline Z$ for its orbit.

The action is free and properly discontinuous; in particular every point has a neighbourhood disjoint from its nonidentity translates. The orbit map $p:\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}\to\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}/W$ is a normal, also called regular, covering with deck group $W$. With first-path-first multiplication on fundamental groups, it induces the exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(\mathcal X^{\mathbb C},Z)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_1(\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}/W,\overline Z)\to W\to1$. The last map records the unique group element carrying $Z$ to the endpoint of the lifted loop.

prop-cover-asphericity-interface-artin-t.title: Coverings preserve the higher-homotopy obstruction to K(pi,1)

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $p:E\to B$ be a covering map with $E$ and $B$ nonempty and path-connected, and choose $e\in E$. For every $n\geq2$, postcomposition with $p$ induces an isomorphism $p_*:\pi_n(E,e)\to\pi_n(B,p(e))$. Here a covering map is a surjective continuous map for which every point of $B$ has an open neighbourhood whose inverse image is a disjoint union of open sets each mapped homeomorphically onto that neighbourhood.

Call a nonempty path-connected space aspherical when all its homotopy groups in degrees at least two vanish. Then $E$ is aspherical if and only if $B$ is aspherical. In particular, if either space is a CW complex and its fundamental group is equipped with a specified isomorphism to $G$, that space is a $K(G,1)$ exactly when it is aspherical. For either $X=E$ or $X=B$, suppose instead that $X$ is of CW homotopy type and has a specified isomorphism $\pi_1(X,x)\cong G$. Then $X$ has the homotopy type of a $K(G,1)$ exactly when it is aspherical. Here being of CW homotopy type means being homotopy equivalent to a CW complex; the equivalence and its inverse homotopies need not preserve basepoints. These statements do not identify the two fundamental groups or supply a finite CW model.

prop-cover-exact-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Vertex-group exact sequence of a normal groupoid cover

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:

A vertex group consists of all arrows from the specified object to itself. Use left-to-right arrow products and ordinary composition of deck functors. Then there is an exact sequence of groups

prop-deligne-ribbon-quotient-artin-tits-.title: Reduced ribbon groupoid is the Deligne orbit quotient

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by $I\subseteq S$, and let $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, whose objects are chamber labels $(x,I)$, and let $\mathcal R$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid. Its objects are the associates of $J$: the subsets $I\subseteq S$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$. The functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple wall crossing of index $a$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$. Let $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ send objects and arrows to their orbits under the normaliser action.

The functor $\mathcal G$ factors as $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\circ\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ is an isomorphism of groupoids. On objects it identifies the $N$-orbits of chambers with the associates of $J$ by $[(x,I)]\mapsto I$.

prop-finite-opposition-interface-artin-t.title: Finite parabolic longest elements and disconnected factors

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite and length function $\ell$. For $I\subseteq S$, write $W_I=\langle I\rangle$, $V_I=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\}$ and $\Phi_I=\{w e_i:w\in W_I,\ i\in I\}$ in the canonical real reflection representation. Put $\Phi_I^+=\Phi_I\cap\Phi_+$ and $\Phi_I^-= -\Phi_I^+$.

If $W_I$ is finite, it has a unique element $w_I$ of maximum length, $w_I^2=1$, and $w_I\Phi_I^+=\Phi_I^-$. There is a permutation $\iota_I$ of $I$ such that $w_Ie_i=-e_{\iota_I(i)}$ for every $i\in I$.

For the connected components $I_1,\ldots,I_k$ of the Coxeter diagram induced on $I$, the factors $W_{I_j}$ commute elementwise, their multiplication map is an isomorphism from their direct product onto $W_I$, and their lengths add. If $W_I$ is finite, each factor is finite and $w_I=\prod_j w_{I_j}$, including the empty product when $I=\varnothing$.

In particular, let $a\in S\setminus I$, put $K=I\cup\{a\}$, and suppose $W_K$ is finite. If $H$ is a union of connected components common to the induced diagrams on $I$ and $K$, write $J=I\setminus H$ and $L=K\setminus H$. Then $w_Iw_K=w_Jw_L$. Thus common disconnected finite factors cancel.

prop-gallery-separation-interface-artin-.title: Finite galleries and separating hyperplanes

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $T$ be an open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real vector space $E$, and let $\mathcal A$ be a locally finite arrangement of linear hyperplanes in $T$. A hyperplane separates two chambers if the chambers lie in opposite open half-spaces bounded by it. Each adjacency in a gallery has a unique defining hyperplane; say the gallery crosses that hyperplane at the adjacency. Any two chambers are joined by a finite gallery. A gallery between them has minimum length if and only if it crosses each separating hyperplane exactly once and crosses no other hyperplane. The minimum length is the number of distinct separating hyperplanes; coincident hyperplanes are counted once.

prop-geodesic-additivity-artin-tits-norm.title: Geodesics are exactly length-additive wall words

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. In its relative chamber arrangement, let $p=((x_1,I_1),\ldots,(x_m,I_m))$ be a nonempty chamber path. For each consecutive pair let $a_i$ be its crossing index and $v_{a_i,I_i}\in W$ its simple wall-crossing element. Put $v_p=v_{a_1,I_1}\cdots v_{a_{m-1},I_{m-1}}$, with the empty product equal to the identity. Write $\ell(w)$ for the least length of a word in the simple generators representing $w$.

The path $p$ is geodesic, meaning that its number of crossings is minimal among paths with the same endpoints, if and only if $\ell(v_p)=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}\ell(v_{a_i,I_i})$. The empty sum is zero.

prop-groupoid-orbit-interface-artin-tits.title: Free object actions give orbit coverings

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let a group $N$ act on a connected small groupoid $G$ by automorphisms, with a left action on objects and arrows: $(nm)a=n(ma)$. Assume that the object action is free, meaning that $nx=x$ implies $n=1$. Arrow products are read left to right. An orbit is the set of translates of an object or arrow.

The object and arrow orbits form a connected groupoid $G/N$: the source and target of an arrow orbit are the orbits of its source and target, and composition is defined by choosing consecutive representatives. For each object $x$, every arrow orbit whose source is $[x]$ has exactly one representative with source $x$. The orbit functor $p:G\to G/N$ is a normal covering, and $n\mapsto(a\mapsto na)$ identifies $N$ with its group of deck transformations, whose multiplication is ordinary function composition.

For every object $x$, there is an exact sequence of groups $1\to G_x\xrightarrow{p}(G/N)_{[x]}\xrightarrow{\delta}N\to1$. Here $G_x$ and $(G/N)_{[x]}$ are the groups of arrows from the indicated object to itself, and $\delta([a])=n$ when the unique representative $a$ with source $x$ has target $nx$. Exactness means that the first map is injective, the last is surjective, and the image of the first equals the kernel of the last.

prop-normaliser-quotient-interface-artin.title: Normalizer quotients, kernels and conditional surjectivity

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$. Its normalizer is $N_G(H)=\{g\in G:gHg^{-1}=H\}$. Then $H$ is normal in $N_G(H)$, so the quotient group $N_G(H)/H$ exists.

Let $p:G\to Q$ be a group homomorphism and put $K=p(H)$. The rule $\bar p(gH)=p(g)K$ defines a homomorphism from $N_G(H)/H$ to $N_Q(K)/K$. Its kernel is $\{aH:a\in\ker p\cap N_G(H)\}$, and its image is $p(N_G(H))/K$. In particular, $\bar p$ is surjective if and only if $p(N_G(H))=N_Q(K)$.

More generally, if $\pi:E\to B$ is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel $M$ and $C\leq E$, then $\pi|_C:C\to B$ is an isomorphism exactly when $E=MC$ and $M\cap C=\{1\}$. Under these conditions $E$ is isomorphic to $M\rtimes B$ by a map compatible with the inclusion of $M$ and the quotient map, with action induced by conjugation through $(\pi|_C)^{-1}$.

prop-parabolic-minimum-interface-artin-t.title: Parabolic root subsystems and unique coset minima

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $S$, presented by a Coxeter matrix, and let $\ell$ be word length in $S$. Let $\rho$ be its canonical real reflection representation on $V=\mathbb R^S$, with basis $(e_s)_{s\in S}$, root system $\Phi=\{\rho(w)e_s:w\in W,s\in S\}$ and positive roots $\Phi_+$, the roots with nonnegative basis coordinates. For $I,K\subseteq S$, write $W_I=\langle I\rangle$, $V_I=\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\}$, $\Phi_I=\{\rho(u)e_i:u\in W_I,i\in I\}$ and $\Phi_I^+=\Phi_I\cap\Phi_+$.

prop-positive-lift-interface-artin-tits-.title: Reduced-word lifts and the prefix-order convention

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, with length $\ell(w)$ equal to the least length of a word in $S$ representing $w$. Let $A$ be its Artin group, generated by $\sigma_s$ for $s\in S$ with the braid relations, and let $\pi:A\to W$ send $\sigma_s$ to $s$. For a reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_r$, meaning one of length $r=\ell(w)$, put $\sigma_w=\sigma_{s_1}\cdots\sigma_{s_r}$, with the empty product equal to the identity. This element is independent of the reduced expression and satisfies $\pi(\sigma_w)=w$. If $\ell(uv)=\ell(u)+\ell(v)$, then $\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\sigma_v$.

For this interface, a left divisor of $v$ means a Coxeter prefix: an element $u$ such that $v=ux$ and $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+\ell(x)$ for some $x\in W$. The relation thus defined is the right weak order $u\le_R v$. The map $w\mapsto\sigma_w$ is a set-theoretic section of $\pi$; it is not asserted to be a homomorphism.

prop-positive-lift-posets-artin-tits-nor.title: Divisibility of positive lifts and weak order

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system of spherical type, meaning that $W$ is finite. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $A^+$ its submonoid generated by the standard generators $\sigma_s$, and $\pi:A\to W$ the homomorphism sending $\sigma_s$ to $s$. Write $\ell(w)$ for the minimum length of a word in $S$ representing $w$. For a reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_r$, define its positive lift by $\sigma_w=\sigma_{s_1}\cdots\sigma_{s_r}$, and put $\widetilde W=\{\sigma_w:w\in W\}\subseteq A^+$.

For $a,b\in A^+$, say that $a$ left-divides $b$ if $b=ac$ for some $c\in A^+$. On $W$ use the prefix weak order: $u\leq v$ if $v=ux$ for some $x\in W$ with $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+\ell(x)$. Restriction of $\pi$ is an isomorphism from $\widetilde W$ with left divisibility to $W$ with this order, with inverse $w\mapsto\sigma_w$. The article calls the latter left weak Bruhat order; the prefix convention here is also called right weak order.

The left-divisibility least common multiple of any two elements of $\widetilde W$ exists in $A^+$ and belongs to $\widetilde W$.

prop-presentation-lifting-interface-arti.title: A criterion for lifting a presented groupoid

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $G$ be the groupoid presented by a small directed graph $Q$, endpoint-preserving path relations $R$, formal inverse edges, and their cancellation relations. Let $(X_x)_{x\in Q_0}$ be a family of sets indexed by the vertex set $Q_0$. For each edge $e:x\to y$ choose a bijection $T_e:X_x\to X_y$, and assign its formal inverse edge the inverse bijection $T_e^{-1}$. Suppose that, for every relation in $R$, the two successive composites of these maps agree on the whole set over its source.

Then there is a small groupoid $E$ with objects the disjoint union of the sets $X_x$ and a functor $p:E\to G$ such that, for each object $u\in X_x$ and each arrow $g$ of $G$ with source $x$, exactly one arrow of $E$ has source $u$ and projects to $g$. The lift of a generating edge sends $u$ to $T_e(u)$. Thus $p$ is a covering in the source-star sense, whether or not $E$ or $G$ is connected. The lifts are determined by the specified maps and the covering property. Equality of projected labels alone does not establish equality of relation lifts: the composites must agree upstairs.

prop-quotient-cover-artin-tits-normalise.title: Quotient groupoids give normal covers

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let a group $N$ act by automorphisms on a connected small groupoid $\mathcal G$, freely on objects. Thus $\mathcal G$ has sets of objects and arrows, every arrow is invertible, and an arrow exists between every ordered pair of objects; freeness means $nx=x$ only for $n=1$. Use the left action and left-to-right arrow composition conventions of [def-groupoid-action-quotient-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-groupoid-action-quotient-artin-tits-normalisers).

Every arrow orbit whose source is the object orbit $[x]$ has a unique representative with source $x$. The object and arrow orbits form a groupoid $\mathcal G/N$, with composition obtained by aligning consecutive representatives. The quotient functor $Q:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/N$ is a normal covering, and $n\mapsto(a\mapsto na)$ is an isomorphism $N\cong\operatorname{Deck}(Q)$, where deck transformations are automorphisms over $Q$. For every object $x$ there is an exact sequence $1\to\mathcal G_x\xrightarrow{Q}(\mathcal G/N)_{[x]}\xrightarrow{\delta}N\to1$, where the vertex groups consist of arrows from the indicated object to itself. If the unique representative of a loop orbit with source $x$ ends at $nx$, then $\delta$ sends that orbit to $n$.

prop-relative-cover-artin-tits-normalise.title: Relative free action, normal cover and exact sequence

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and $J\subseteq S$. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and let $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified complement of [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). The induced diagonal $N(W,J)$-action on $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ is free and properly discontinuous: every point has an open neighbourhood disjoint from all its nonidentity translates.

The quotient map is a normal covering, meaning a covering whose deck transformations act transitively on every fibre. For $x\in\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ and its image $\overline x$, it induces the exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C},x)\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}/N(W,J),\overline x)\to N(W,J)\to1$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication; the last map sends a loop to the unique element taking $x$ to the endpoint of its lift starting at $x$.

prop-relative-linear-interface-artin-tit.title: Annihilators, relative hyperplanes and complexification

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $V$ be a real vector space with finite basis $(e_s)_{s\in S}$, let $J\subseteq S$, and let $E=\{f\in V^*:f(e_j)=0\text{ for every }j\in J\}$. For $\alpha\in V$, write $r_\alpha:E\to\mathbb R$ for the restricted evaluation $r_\alpha(f)=f(\alpha)$. Then $r_\alpha$ is zero exactly when $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}\{e_j:j\in J\}$; otherwise its kernel is a linear hyperplane of $E$, meaning that its quotient in $E$ has dimension one. Two nonzero restricted evaluations have the same kernel exactly when one is a nonzero real scalar multiple of the other.

Identify the complexification $E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ with $E\oplus iE$ by $f\otimes(a+bi)\mapsto af+i bf$. For a real hyperplane $H\subseteq E$, its complexification, understood as the image of $H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ under the inclusion into $E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, is $H\oplus iH$.

For subsets of $E$, relative interior and closure mean interior and closure computed in $E$ with the metric induced by the coordinate Euclidean metric on $V^*$ associated to the basis $(e_s)$. Thus balls used in these operations are balls in $E$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $\Gamma_0$ be finite, $W$ its Coxeter group, $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$, and use the relative space $E=\Theta_J$, Tits cone intersection $T=\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, and set of distinct relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$ from [def-relative-cone-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-cone-artin-tits-normalisers). The interior $T^\circ$ is taken in $E$. Every $u\in T^\circ$ has an open ball in $T$ meeting only finitely many hyperplanes of $\mathcal H^J$. In particular $(T^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$ is locally finite, with the hyperplane set restricted to the members meeting $T^\circ$.

prop-relative-stratification-artin-tits-.title: Convexity, stratification and faces of the relative cone

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite generating set, in its canonical real reflection representation on $V$ with simple-root basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in S}$ and dual space $\Theta$. For $L\subseteq S$, let $W_L$ be the subgroup generated by $L$, let $\Theta_L=\{f\in\Theta:f(\alpha_i)=0\text{ for }i\in L\}$, and let $C_L$ consist of the points of $\Theta_L$ that are positive on every $\alpha_i$ with $i\notin L$. Let $H_\alpha=\{f:f(\alpha)=0\}$ and let $\mathrm{Cone}=\bigcup_{x\in W}x\overline{C_\varnothing}$. Fix $J\subseteq S$ and put $\mathrm{Cone}(J)=\mathrm{Cone}\cap\Theta_J$. Its relative arrangement consists of the distinct hyperplanes $H_\alpha\cap\Theta_J$ for roots $\alpha$ whose hyperplanes do not contain $\Theta_J$. A chamber is a connected component of the complement of these hyperplanes in $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$; closures below are taken in $\Theta_J$.

The set $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$ is a convex cone and is the disjoint union of the sets $xC_L$ indexed by $L\subseteq S$ and $x\in W/W_L$ for which $xC_L\subseteq\Theta_J$. Its chambers are exactly those sets in this union with $|L|=|J|$. For such a chamber, its codimension-one faces are $xC_{L+i}$ for $i\in S\setminus L$, where $L+i=L\cup\{i\}$. The corresponding wall is the closure of this face and satisfies $\overline{xC_{L+i}}=H_{x\alpha_i}\cap\overline{xC_L}$; its supporting relative hyperplane is $H_{x\alpha_i}\cap\Theta_J$. When $J=\varnothing$, the same formula gives the stratification of the full Tits cone.

prop-ribbon-lcm-relations-artin-tits-nor.title: Two ribbon-lcm expressions and presentation

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram with vertex set $S$, let $A^+$ be its positive Artin monoid, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Use the reduced ribbon groupoid $\mathcal R(J)$ and elementary arrows $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_{I\cup\{a\}}:I\to K$ of [def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers), where $I$ ranges over the associates of $J$ and $a\in S\setminus I$. Thus an associate means a subset whose standard parabolic Coxeter subgroup is conjugate to that of $J$.

For distinct $a,b\in S\setminus I$, the least common multiple $\mu_{a,I}\vee\mu_{b,I}$ for left divisibility in $A^+$ is represented by a morphism of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $I$. It has exactly two expressions as composable products of elementary arrows: one begins with $\mu_{a,I}$ and the other with $\mu_{b,I}$. If their lengths are $m$ and $n$, respectively, these expressions have the form $\mu_{a_1,I_1}\cdots\mu_{a_m,I_m}$ and $\mu_{b_1,L_1}\cdots\mu_{b_n,L_n}$, with $a_1=a$, $b_1=b$, and $I_1=L_1=I$.

The elementary arrows, their formal inverses, and the groupoid identity and inverse laws generate $\mathcal R(J)$, and the equalities between these two expressions, over all associates $I$ and all distinct pairs $a,b\in S\setminus I$, give a complete set of defining relations. For $a=b$, the lcm is $\mu_{a,I}$ and has one elementary-arrow expression; the corresponding equality is tautological.

prop-root-inversion-interface-artin-tits.title: Root signs, inversions and descent translation

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $S$ be finite and let $(W,S)$, $V$, its basis $(e_s)_{s\in S}$, the Coxeter form $B$, the canonical representation, the root set $\Phi$, the dual action, and the open chamber $C^\circ$ be as in the canonical real Coxeter interface. Let $\ell(w)$ be the minimum length of a word in $S$ representing $w$. Put $V_+=\{\sum_{s\in S}a_se_s:a_s\geq0\}$ and $\Phi_+=\Phi\cap V_+$. A root in $-\Phi_+$ is called negative.

Every root has exactly one sign: $\Phi=\Phi_+\sqcup(-\Phi_+)$. For $N(w)=\{\alpha\in\Phi_+:w\alpha\in-\Phi_+\}$ one has $|N(w)|=\ell(w)=\ell(w^{-1})$. For $s\in S$, the chamber $wC^\circ$ lies in $\{f:f(e_s)<0\}$ exactly when $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, equivalently when $w^{-1}e_s$ is negative.

For a root $\alpha$, write $H_\alpha=\{f\in V^*:f(\alpha)=0\}$. Distinct positive roots have distinct full hyperplanes $H_\alpha$. The map $\alpha\mapsto H_\alpha\cap U$ need not be injective when restricted to a real linear subspace $U\subseteq V^*$.

prop-root-length-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Root-sign and inversion-length facts

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be the Coxeter system of the stated Coxeter diagram, with geometric representation on $V=\bigoplus_{i\in\Gamma_0}\mathbb R\alpha_i$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+=\Phi\cap\sum_i\mathbb R_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, negative roots $\Phi^-=-\Phi^+$, length $\ell$, and contragredient action on the algebraic dual $V^*$. The index set may be infinite.

The roots decompose as $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup\Phi^-$. The contragredient action faithfully realizes $W$ as a group generated by linear reflections. For $w\in W$, $\ell(w)=|\{\alpha\in\Phi^+:w\alpha\in\Phi^-\}|=\ell(w^{-1})$. If $w^{-1}\alpha_i\in\Phi^-$, then $\ell(s_iw)=\ell(w^{-1}s_i)<\ell(w)$.

prop-sign-chamber-interface-artin-tits-p.title: Sign cells and local finite-arrangement reductions

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with its Euclidean topology, and let $T\subseteq E$ be open and convex. Let $\mathcal A$ be a set of distinct linear hyperplanes, each meeting $T$, locally finite in $T$: each point of $T$ has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many members. For each $H\in\mathcal A$, choose a nonzero linear functional $a_H:E\to\mathbb R$ with kernel $H$. A chamber is a connected component of $T\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal A}H$.

For any assignment $\epsilon_H\in\{1,-1\}$, the corresponding strict sign cell is $C_\epsilon=\{x\in T:\epsilon_Ha_H(x)>0\text{ for every }H\in\mathcal A\}$. Every nonempty sign cell is a convex chamber, and every chamber is a sign cell.

For a chamber $C=C_\epsilon$ and a point $p\in\overline C\cap T$, there is an open convex neighbourhood $U$ of $p$ contained in $T$ that meets $C$ and only finitely many hyperplanes. For every such $U$, writing $\mathcal A_U=\{H\in\mathcal A:H\cap U\ne\varnothing\}$, one has $\overline C\cap U=\{x\in U:\epsilon_Ha_H(x)\geq0\text{ for all }H\in\mathcal A_U\}$. Here $\overline C$ denotes closure in $E$. In particular, if a wall is an intersection $\overline C\cap H_0$ of affine dimension $\dim E-1$ for $H_0\in\mathcal A$, its intersection with $U$ is described by these finitely many weak inequalities together with $a_{H_0}=0$; it is empty if $H_0$ does not meet $U$. No neighbourhood assertion at a boundary point outside $T$ is made.

prop-tits-cone-basic-artin-tits-normalis.title: Basic Tits-cone properties

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite, with the canonical real reflection representation, its dual space $\Theta$, the contragredient $W$-action, the closed fundamental chamber $\overline C$, the Tits cone $\mathrm{Cone}=\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C$, and the set $\mathcal H$ of distinct root hyperplanes as in [def-coxeter-arrangement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-coxeter-arrangement-artin-tits-normalisers). Use the finite-dimensional topology specified there.

The Tits cone is a $W$-invariant convex cone. The chamber $\overline C$ is a fundamental domain in the sense that every $W$-orbit in $\mathrm{Cone}$ meets it in exactly one point. The arrangement $(\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ},\mathcal H)$ is locally finite: every point of $\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ}$ has a neighbourhood in $\Theta$ meeting only finitely many members of $\mathcal H$. Finally, $W$ is finite if and only if $\mathrm{Cone}=\Theta$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite, in its canonical real reflection representation on $V=\mathbb R^S$, with basis $(e_s)_{s\in S}$, root system $\Phi$ and positive roots $\Phi_+$. Let $\Theta=V^*$ carry the contragredient action. Put $\overline C=\{f\in\Theta:f(e_s)\geq 0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$ and $U=\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C$. For $I\subseteq S$, let $C_I$ be the set of points of $\overline C$ whose zero coordinates are exactly those indexed by $I$, and let $W_I$ be the subgroup generated by $I$. The root hyperplane of $\alpha\in\Phi$ is $H_\alpha=\{f:f(\alpha)=0\}$; interiors and neighborhoods use the ordinary finite-dimensional topology on $\Theta$.

A functional $f$ belongs to $U$ exactly when $\{\alpha\in\Phi_+:f(\alpha)<0\}$ is finite. The cone $U$ is convex, and $\overline C$ meets each $W$-orbit in $U$ exactly once. In general local finiteness of chambers does not extend to boundary points: if $W$ is infinite, every neighborhood of $0$ meets infinitely many distinct chambers $w\overline C$.

prop-topological-orbit-interface-artin-t.title: Covering-space actions and fundamental-groupoid quotients

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let a group $N$ act on a nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected space $X$ by homeomorphisms, with every point having an open neighbourhood disjoint from all its nonidentity translates. Give $B=X/N$ the quotient topology and write $p:X\to B$ for the orbit map. Then $p$ is a regular covering: its deck transformations act transitively on each fibre. Its deck group is precisely $N$, acting as given.

The induced action on the fundamental groupoid $\Pi_1(X)$ sends points and endpoint-fixed path classes to their translates. Its orbit groupoid has object and arrow orbits, with composition defined by choosing representatives whose endpoints agree. Projection induces an isomorphism $\Pi_1(X)/N\cong\Pi_1(B)$. The induced functor $\Pi_1(X)\to\Pi_1(B)$ is a groupoid covering: for each point upstairs, it bijects the arrows starting there with the arrows starting at its image.

For $x\in X$, use first-path-first multiplication on fundamental groups. The endpoint of the lift of a loop at $p(x)$ starting at $x$ is $n x$ for a unique $n\in N$; this defines the last map in the exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\xrightarrow{p_*}\pi_1(B,p(x))\to N\to1$. No universal cover is used here. Semilocal simple connectedness is a separate local condition to be checked when invoking the usual universal-cover existence theorem.

prop-topological-quotient-groupoid-artin.title: Fundamental groupoids of free topological quotients

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $X$ be a nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected space. Thus any two points of $X$ can be joined by a path; each point has a basis of path-connected neighbourhoods; and each point has a neighbourhood whose inclusion sends every based loop in that neighbourhood to a null-homotopic loop in $X$. Let a group $N$ act on $X$ by homeomorphisms, freely and properly discontinuously, in the following sense: for each $x\in X$ there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $nU\cap U=\varnothing$ for every nonidentity $n\in N$. Write $p:X\to X/N$ for the orbit map, with the quotient topology on $X/N$.

Then $p$ is a normal covering: it is a covering map and its deck transformations, the homeomorphisms $h:X\to X$ satisfying $p\circ h=p$, act transitively on each fibre. The induced functor $p_*:\Pi_1(X)\to\Pi_1(X/N)$ is a groupoid covering: for every $x\in X$, it bijects the arrows starting at $x$ with those starting at $p(x)$. Here $\Pi_1$ has points as objects and endpoint-fixed path-homotopy classes as arrows, composed by concatenation.

The action of $N$ on points and path classes induces an action by groupoid automorphisms on $\Pi_1(X)$. Its quotient $\Pi_1(X)/N$ has object and arrow orbits, with composition defined by aligning representatives. Projection induces a canonical isomorphism $\overline p_*:\Pi_1(X)/N\to\Pi_1(X/N)$, and $p_*=\overline p_*\circ Q$, where $Q$ is the orbit functor. Thus the two groupoid coverings agree under this canonical identification.

prop-universal-generators-artin-tits-nor.title: The universal wall groupoid is generated by adjacent crossings

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Let $\Theta_J=\{f:f(\alpha_j)=0\text{ for every }j\in J\}$, let $\mathrm{Cone}(J)=\mathrm{Cone}\cap\Theta_J$, and let $\mathcal H^J$ be the set of distinct proper root-hyperplane traces on $\Theta_J$. Here $\mathrm{Cone}$ is the Tits cone, and $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ$ is the interior in $\Theta_J$. A chamber is a connected component of the arrangement complement, and distinct chambers are adjacent when they share a wall.

Write $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ for the pairs $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ of minimum length in $xW_I$. The chamber-labelling bijection identifies these pairs with the chambers of $(\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$. Restriction from the full relative cone to its interior identifies the chambers and preserves adjacency. The universal wall groupoid $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ has these labels as objects; for $A=(x,I)$ and $B=(y,K)$ its unique arrow is the endpoint-tagged triple $(A,B,x^{-1}y)$. Composition multiplies labels from left to right.

For any $A,B\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ there is a finite chamber path $p=\omega_{a_1,I_1}*\cdots*\omega_{a_m,I_m}:A\to B$ in the relative-interior arrangement $(\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$, consisting of simple wall crossings between adjacent chambers. Its wall word is $v_p=v_{a_1,I_1}\cdots v_{a_m,I_m}=x^{-1}y\in W$. Defining the tagged arrow $[p]=(A,B,v_p)$, we have $\operatorname{Hom}_{\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)}(A,B)=\{[p]\}$; after taking arrow labels this singleton is $\{v_p\}$. The path need not be unique. If $A=B$, it may be the one-chamber path of length zero, with $v_p=1$. Thus the adjacent-crossing morphisms generate the groupoid.

prop-weak-order-interface-artin-tits-pre.title: Bounded weak-order joins and finite parabolic criteria

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(S,m)$ be a Coxeter matrix on a finite set, $W$ its presented Coxeter group, and $\ell(w)$ the minimum length of a word in $S$ representing $w$. The prefix order on $W$ is $u\preceq v$ exactly when $v=ux$ for some $x\in W$ with $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+\ell(x)$. An upper bound of $A\subseteq W$ is an element above every member of $A$; a join is an upper bound lying below every upper bound. Dually, a meet is a lower bound lying above every lower bound.

Every nonempty subset of $W$ has a meet, and a subset has a join exactly when it has an upper bound. If $W$ is finite, this order is a lattice, meaning that every pair has a meet and join, with top element $w_S$, the unique element of maximum length in $W$.

For $I\subseteq S$, put $W_I=\langle s:s\in I\rangle$. The set $I$ has a join exactly when $W_I$ is finite; then its join is $w_I$, the unique element of maximum length in $W_I$. This includes $I=\varnothing$, for which $w_I=1$. Thus a join in an infinite system is asserted only when its set is bounded above.

rem-action-not-transitive-artin-tits-nor.title: The relative normaliser action need not be chamber-transitive

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, and fix $J\subseteq S$. For $I\subseteq S$, let $W_I$ be the subgroup generated by $I$, and let $\ell$ be word length in $S$. A chamber label is a pair $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ for which $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. The normaliser quotient $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ acts on these labels, and hence on the corresponding relative chambers. An action is transitive if any chamber can be carried to any other by an acting element.

When $J=\varnothing$, this action is transitive. In general it need not be transitive: for type $A_2$, with $S=\{s,t\}$, $m(s,t)=3$ and $J=\{s\}$, the labels $(1,\{s\})$ and $(ts,\{t\})$ lie in different orbits.

rem-arrangement-to-universal-artin-tits-.title: Natural functors to the universal wall groupoid

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and fix a subset $J$ of its diagram vertices. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and let $\mathcal D(J)$ be its groupoid completion. Its chambers have labels $(x,I)$, where $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Use the chamber-labelling bijection to identify these chambers with their algebraic labels. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ be the groupoid with one arrow from each label $(x,I)$ to each label $(y,K)$, labelled $x^{-1}y$.

There are full functors $\mathcal D^+(J)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ and $\mathcal D(J)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$, both identity on objects. The first sends a chamber path $p:(x,I)\to(y,K)$ to its wall word $v_p=x^{-1}y$; the second extends the first and sends formal inverses to inverses. Every based loop in either source maps to the identity. If the arrangement has two adjacent chambers, neither functor is faithful. statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and fix a subset $J$ of its diagram vertices. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and let $\mathcal D(J)$ be its groupoid completion. Its chambers have labels $(x,I)$, where $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Use the chamber-labelling bijection to identify these chambers with their algebraic labels. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ be the groupoid with one arrow from each label $(x,I)$ to each label $(y,K)$, labelled $x^{-1}y$.

There are full functors $\mathcal D^+(J)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ and $\mathcal D(J)\to\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$, both identity on objects. The first sends a chamber path $p:(x,I)\to(y,K)$ to its wall word $v_p=x^{-1}y$; the second extends the first and sends formal inverses to inverses. Every based loop in either source maps to the identity. If the arrangement has two adjacent chambers, neither functor is faithful. Here full means surjective on every hom-set, and faithful means injective on every hom-set.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, let $\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}$ be its classical complexified arrangement complement, and let $A=\pi_1(\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}/W)$ be the associated Artin–Tits group. The classical $K(\pi,1)$ assertion says that $\mathcal X^{\mathbb C}/W$ is a classifying space for $A$: it has fundamental group $A$ and contractible universal cover. Here the quotient uses the universal-cover convention for $K(A,1)$. Its Salvetti quotient is a connected CW model $C$ homotopy equivalent to it; equivalently, $\pi_1(C)\cong A$ with the induced group identification and $\pi_n(C)=0$ for every $n>1$, so $C$ is a $K(A,1)$ in the CW-complex definition.

The article reports this assertion as proved for spherical, FC and affine types, and cites further cases [11,19,23] without specifying them in that paragraph. Spherical type means that $W$ is finite. FC type means that every subset $T\subseteq S$ for which all Coxeter labels $m(s,t)$ with $s,t\in T$ are finite generates a finite subgroup $W_T$.

A Coxeter system is irreducible when its Coxeter diagram is connected. An irreducible system is affine when its Coxeter form $B$ is positive semidefinite of corank one, as in the affine-form convention. The standard diagrams in the four families are $\widetilde A_n$ for $n\geq1$, $\widetilde B_n$ for $n\geq3$, $\widetilde C_n$ for $n\geq2$, and $\widetilde D_n$ for $n\geq4$; the exceptional types are $\widetilde E_6$, $\widetilde E_7$, $\widetilde E_8$, $\widetilde F_4$, and $\widetilde G_2$. These exhaust the irreducible affine systems. Here the names denote the standard labelled Coxeter diagrams, including the two-vertex infinity-labelled diagram $\widetilde A_1$.

For disconnected systems, use the componentwise convention: affine type means a nonempty finite disjoint union of irreducible affine diagrams. The assertion holds for these reducible affine cases as well, and also when spherical components are included. The finite-product deduction is given below; the irreducible affine theorem is an imported result.
