statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: A subset $L$ is **finitary** when its standard parabolic subgroup $W_L$ is finite. For finitary objects $I,K$, taking minimum-length representatives identifies core cosets $W_IxW_K$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{BH}}(I,K)$. For an atom put $L=I+a$; its deleted target vertex is $a'=\iota_L(a)=\iota_{[I,a]}(a)$ and its minimum is $v_{a,I}=w_Iw_L$, while its maximum is $w_L$. Atomic reduced expressions correspond to standard expressions, and Ko's atomic braid relations correspond exactly to the BH atomic braid relations. Consequently Ko's atomic Matsumoto theorem is the finitary restriction of the BH atomic Matsumoto theorem. The latter also permits infinite objects $I$: only the crossing component $[I,a]$ is required to be spherical, and $W_{I+a}$ need not be finite.

rem-d4-normaliser-action-wording-artin-t.title: Normaliser-action wording in the D4 exposition

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
In the $D_4$ example, vertex $2$ is central, $J=\{2\}$, and $W_J=\langle s_2\rangle$. The normaliser is $\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)=\{g\in W:gW_Jg^{-1}=W_J\}$ and $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. A relative chamber has a unique label $(x,I)$ satisfying $W_Jx=xW_I$ and with $x$ of minimum length in $xW_I$; it is the face translate $xC_I$.

The induced action of $N(W,J)$ on these chambers is free: a quotient element fixing a chamber is the identity. Two chambers are in the same orbit, meaning that one is the image of the other under a quotient element, exactly when their second labels agree. There are four orbits, indexed by $I=\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{4\}$, each containing eight chambers.

The article's paragraph instead says that the action of each $g\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$ is free. The quotient formulation above makes the intended freeness precise: the nonidentity element $s_2$ acts trivially on every relative chamber.

rem-d4-region-poset-artin-tits-normalise.title: D4 grading, region poset and simple-morphism divisibility

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
The $D_4$ chamber graph is graded by distance from $C=(e,2)$, equivalently by standard-expression length $\ell_{\mathcal{BH}}(x)$ for a label $(x,I)$. Here a standard expression is a composable factorisation into simple wall-crossing morphisms whose Coxeter lengths add to the Coxeter length of their product. The notation $\ell_{\mathcal{BH}}(x)$ means the common number of factors in standard expressions for $x:\{2\}\to I$; its independence of the expression is verified below. Singleton second labels are abbreviated, so $(x,i)$ means $(x,\{i\})$. Define the region order by $A\leq B$ if $S(A)\subseteq S(B)$, where $S(A)$ is the subset of the seven arrangement hyperplanes that separate $C$ from $A$. Its Hasse diagram, meaning its graph of cover relations, is this graded chamber graph. Its minimum is $C$ and its maximum is $-C=(stuvtsutvtu,2)$. It is also the left-divisibility diagram of simple arrows with source $C$ in the positive Garside category underlying $\mathcal D$.

The underlying graph agrees with Ko's diagram immediately before Remark 8.6, with the vertical orientation reversed. The full correspondence is given below. The chamber colours record second labels: black $1$, red $2$, green $3$, blue $4$. Together with the specified base chamber and the edges of the diagram, these uniquely determine all chamber labels. Ko's original diagram is monochrome; its numerical labels count reduced atomic expressions and are not chamber colours.

source_references.statement: A complete-local complex cDV ring is a hypersurface deformation of a Du Val surface. Crepancy means pullback equality of canonical sheaves. For a crepant partial resolution of a cDV singularity, a generic section gives a partial resolution of an ADE surface, dominated by its minimal resolution. rem-disjoint-interiors-artin-tits-normal.title: Relative cones can avoid the interior of the full cone

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S$ finite, with canonical real representation on $V$, simple roots $(e_s)_{s\in S}$ and dual space $\Theta=V^*$ as in [def-real-coxeter-interface-artin-tits-prerequisites](item-def-real-coxeter-interface-artin-tits-prerequisites). Let $J\subseteq S$ and $W_J=\langle J\rangle$. Write $\Theta_J=\{f\in\Theta:f(e_j)=0\text{ for every }j\in J\}$, let $\mathrm{Cone}$ be the union of the $W$-translates of the closed fundamental chamber, and put $\mathrm{Cone}(J)=\mathrm{Cone}\cap\Theta_J$ as in [def-relative-cone-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-cone-artin-tits-normalisers). The superscript $\circ$ denotes interior in the indicated ambient space: $\Theta$ for $\mathrm{Cone}$ and $\Theta_J$ for $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$.

Although $\mathrm{Cone}(J)\subseteq\mathrm{Cone}$, the relative cone can be disjoint from $\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ}$. Indeed, if $W_J$ is infinite, then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)\cap\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ}=\varnothing$, and hence $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ$ is also disjoint from $\mathrm{Cone}^{\circ}$. Consequently the relative interior arrangement need not be a restriction of the full interior arrangement, so its local finiteness does not immediately follow by restricting the latter. The general proof of relative local finiteness also applies to $J=\varnothing$, where it gives the full interior arrangement.

rem-empty-j-presentation-artin-tits-norm.title: The ordinary Coxeter presentation is the empty-J case

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with generators $S=\{s_i:i\in\Gamma_0\}$ and Coxeter matrix $m$, and let $J=\varnothing$. Its Brink–Howlett groupoid has one object, $\varnothing$, and its endomorphism group is $W$. Each elementary wall-crossing arrow $v_{a,\varnothing}$ has label $s_a$.

For distinct vertices $a,b$, the two-generator arrow $v_{a,b,\varnothing}$ is defined precisely when $s_as_b$ has finite order $m=m(s_a,s_b)$. In that case its label is the longest element of $W_{\{a,b\}}=\langle s_a,s_b\rangle$, represented by each of the two alternating words of length $m$, one beginning with $s_a$ and the other with $s_b$. The atomic braid relation equates these two words. The Brink–Howlett presentation therefore specializes to the Coxeter presentation: generators $s_a$, relations $s_a^2=1$, and the alternating braid relation of length $m(s_a,s_b)$ for each distinct pair with finite matrix entry.

rem-finite-classifying-complexes-artin-t.title: Finite CW-models for spherical normaliser quotients

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system and $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $P$ its pure subgroup, and $N(P,J),N(A,J)$ and $G=N(W,J)$ the normaliser quotients, with $N(P,J)$ the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$. Put $E=\Theta_J$, let $\mathcal H^J$ be the relative hyperplane arrangement, and put $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$.

Choose the finite Salvetti CW model $K=\operatorname{Sal}(E,\mathcal H^J)$ to be the weak geometric realization of the order complex of the incident-facet/chamber poset. It admits a $G$-equivariant homotopy equivalence $f:K\to X$. The induced map $\bar f:K/G\to X/G$ is a homotopy equivalence and its source is a finite CW complex. Here equivariance means $f(gk)=g f(k)$; the homotopy equivalences are ordinary homotopy equivalences and orbit spaces have the quotient topology. Consequently $K$ and $K/G$ are finite classifying-space models for $N(P,J)$ and $N(A,J)$ respectively. A finite CW complex has finitely many cells, and a $K(H,1)$ is a nonempty path-connected space with fundamental group isomorphic to $H$ and trivial homotopy groups in degrees at least two.

rem-groupoid-square-artin-tits-normalise.title: Commutative square of arrangement, ribbon and Brink–Howlett groupoids

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_J$ for the subgroup generated by $J$ and $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. The relative arrangement groupoid $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ has relative chambers as objects and is generated by directed crossings of adjacent chambers and their inverses, with geodesic paths having the same endpoints identified. The universal wall groupoid $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}$ has chamber labels $(x,I)$ as objects and exactly one arrow between any ordered pair, labelled $x^{-1}y$ from $(x,I)$ to $(y,K)$. The Brink–Howlett groupoid $\mathcal{BH}$ has the associates of $J$ as objects, where $I$ is an associate when $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$, and arrows $I\to K$ are the elements carrying the simple-root set of $K$ onto that of $I$.

For arbitrary Coxeter type, the natural functors $H:\mathcal D\to\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}$ and $\mathcal F:\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}\to\mathcal{BH}$ exist; $H$ is the identity on chamber objects and $\mathcal F$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and the arrow labelled $x^{-1}y$ to the same element of $W$.

Suppose now that $W$ is finite, also called spherical type. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, $A_I$ its standard parabolic subgroup, and $\pi:A\to W$ the homomorphism sending each Artin generator to its corresponding simple reflection. The reduced ribbon groupoid $\mathcal R$ has the associates of $J$ as objects and is generated by elementary ribbons $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_{I\cup\{a\}}$ and their inverses, where $a\in S\setminus I$ and $\Delta_L$ is the positive lift of the longest element of $W_L$. The functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and each directed crossing indexed by $a$ at $(x,I)$ to $\mu_{a,I}$.

The homomorphism $\pi$ induces a functor $P:\mathcal R\to\mathcal{BH}$, identity on objects, sending $\mu_{a,I}$ to the corresponding wall-crossing element $v_{a,I}$. The square commutes: $P\mathcal G=\mathcal F H$. Both vertical functors $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$ are normal coverings with deck group isomorphic to $N(W,J)$. A covering has a unique lift from each specified source object for each arrow starting at its image; it is normal when its deck transformations act transitively on a fibre, and a deck transformation is an automorphism over the covering.

At the chamber labelled $(1,J)$ and its image $J$, the respective vertex groups of $\mathcal D$, $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}$, $\mathcal R$ and $\mathcal{BH}$ are isomorphic to $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C},x)$, the trivial group, $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$, and $N(W,J)$. Here $x$ is a chamber basepoint corresponding to $(1,J)$ under the arrangement-groupoid equivalence, and $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ is the relative complexified hyperplane complement.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, with simple roots $(e_s)_{s\in S}$ in its canonical real reflection representation and contragredient action on the dual. For $I\subseteq S$, let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ and let $C_I$ be the face consisting of dual functionals that vanish on $e_i$ for $i\in I$ and are positive on $e_s$ for $s\notin I$. If $x'\in xW_I$, then $x'C_I=xC_I$; consequently distinct group elements can give the same face translate.

Fix $J\subseteq S$. A label in $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ is a pair $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ of minimum word length in $xW_I$. These labels identify the chambers of the relative arrangement in the interior of the $J$-cone bijectively with their face translates $xC_I$. Thus the minimum-length condition removes the ambiguity within each right coset, and distinct labels do not describe the same chamber. Accordingly $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ may denote either this label set or the corresponding set of geometric chambers, with the bijection understood.

rem-normaliser-deligne-action-artin-tits.title: Induced normaliser action on arrangement groupoids

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and let $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_J$ for the subgroup generated by $J$ and $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ for its normaliser quotient. Let $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ be the relative chamber set and let $\mathcal D(J)$ be its arrangement groupoid. A simple wall crossing $\omega_{a,I}:C\to C'$ is the directed generating arrow across the indicated wall, where the chamber label of $C$ has second component $I$ and $a$ is the crossing index.

The action of $N(W,J)$ on chambers induces an action by automorphisms of $\mathcal D(J)$. For $g\in N(W,J)$ it sends $\omega_{a,I}:C\to C'$ to the simple wall crossing $\omega_{a,I}:gC\to gC'$. It preserves geodesic paths and hence the defining relations of the positive arrangement category.

rem-normaliser-equivalence-chain-artin-t.title: Explicit equivalence chain for the middle isomorphism

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, and let $W_J$ and $A_J$ be the subgroups generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$. Put $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(H)=\{g\in G:gHg^{-1}=H\}$.

Let $\mathcal R=\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid, whose objects are the subsets $I\subseteq S$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$, and let $\mathcal R_J$ be its vertex group at $J$: the group of arrows $J\to J$. Let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ be the groupoid completion of the positive relative chamber category. Put $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ for the relative complexified arrangement complement and $N=N(W,J)$.

Write $E=\Theta_J$ for the subspace of the dual Coxeter representation on which the simple roots indexed by $J$ vanish. For $n=gW_J\in N$ with $g\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$, let $n$ act on $E$ by the restricted contragredient action: $(nf)(v)=f(g^{-1}v)$. This is independent of the lift $g$ because $W_J$ fixes $E$ pointwise. Use its diagonal extension $n\cdot(u,v)=(gu,gv)$ on $X\subseteq E\times E$; the action permutes the relative hyperplanes, so it preserves $X$. On a chamber label $(w,I)$, where $W_Jw=wW_I$ and $w$ has minimum Coxeter length in $wW_I$, the action is $n\cdot(w,I)=(y,I)$, where $y$ is the unique minimum-length element of $gwW_I$. On $\mathcal D$ it sends each directed crossing $C\to C'$ to the crossing $nC\to nC'$ with the same wall index, and extends to composites and inverses. This action preserves the geodesic relations. The notation $X/N$ denotes the topological orbit space for the diagonal action, and $\mathcal D/N$ denotes the orbit groupoid for this action on objects and arrows. The corresponding action on $\Pi_1(X)$ sends a path class $[\gamma]$ to $[n\circ\gamma]$.

Let $d=(e,J)$ be the standard chamber object of $\mathcal D$, let $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$ be the equivariant equivalence, and set $x=p(d)$ and $\bar x$ equal to the image of $x$ in $X/N$. Here $\Pi_1(Y)$ is the groupoid of points of $Y$ and endpoint-fixed homotopy classes of paths, and $\pi_1(Y,y)$ is its vertex group at $y$.

The middle isomorphism in the algebraic-to-topological exact-sequence comparison is obtained on vertex groups from the equivalence chain $N(A,J)\simeq\mathcal R\xrightarrow{(\mathcal G')^{-1}}\mathcal D/N\xrightarrow{\bar p}\Pi_1(X/N)\simeq\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)$. The first equivalence uses the spherical ribbon splitting, and the last passes to a vertex group. The groups at the two ends are regarded as one-object groupoids. The displayed arrows involving $\mathcal G'$ and $\bar p$ are, respectively, the inverse of the Deligne-to-ribbon quotient isomorphism and the equivalence induced by $p$.

rem-relative-salvetti-artin-tits-normali.title: Relative Salvetti models and the finiteness qualification

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $S$ and $J\subseteq S$. For the relative complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ of [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers), assume its cone interior is nonempty. The locally finite relative arrangement of [prop-relative-local-finiteness-artin-tits-normalisers](item-prop-relative-local-finiteness-artin-tits-normalisers) has a Salvetti CW model homotopy equivalent to $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$, by [thm-salvetti-topology-input-artin-tits-prerequisites](item-thm-salvetti-topology-input-artin-tits-prerequisites). This model is finite whenever the relative arrangement is finite; in particular it is finite when $W$ is finite. Local finiteness alone does not imply finite CW homotopy type: for $W=\langle s,t\mid s^2=t^2=1\rangle$ and $J=\varnothing$, there is no finite CW model, as established in [lem-author-6f173a9d0001-finite-cw-obstruction](item-lem-author-6f173a9d0001-finite-cw-obstruction).

rem-same-chambers-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Interior restriction preserves chambers and adjacency

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite generating set and $J\subseteq S$. Put $E=\Theta_J$, $T=\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, and let $T^\circ$ denote the interior of $T$ in $E$. Let $\mathcal H^J$ be the set of distinct relative root hyperplanes. Restricting the arrangement from $T$ to $T^\circ$ identifies their chambers and preserves adjacency. The interior arrangement is locally finite, and any two of its chambers are joined by a finite gallery, meaning a finite sequence of chambers in which consecutive chambers are adjacent.

rem-spherical-garside-artin-tits-normali.title: Garside divisibility and lcm assertions for A+

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$. Let $A^+$ be the submonoid of the associated Artin–Tits group $A$ generated by its standard generators. Then $A^+$ is a Garside monoid and every pair of its elements has a greatest common divisor and a least common multiple for each of left and right divisibility.

In particular, let $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and let $I$ be an associate of $J$: thus $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and the standard parabolic subgroups $W_I$ and $W_J$ are conjugate in $W$. For $a,b\in I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$, the positive elementary ribbon elements $\mu_{a,I},\mu_{b,I}\in A^+$ have a left-divisibility least common multiple $\mu_{a,I}\vee\mu_{b,I}$ in $A^+$.

Then $A^+$ is a Garside monoid and every pair of its elements has a greatest common divisor and a least common multiple for each of left and right divisibility.

In particular, let $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and let $I$ be an associate of $J$: thus $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and the standard parabolic subgroups $W_I$ and $W_J$ are conjugate in $W$. For $a,b\in I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$, the positive elementary ribbon elements $\mu_{a,I},\mu_{b,I}\in A^+$ have a left-divisibility least common multiple $\mu_{a,I}\vee\mu_{b,I}$ in $A^+$.

rem-threefold-flop-applications-artin-ti.title: Threefold-flop realization of relative arrangements and derived actions

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
The relative arrangements discussed by the article occur in the homological minimal model programme for threefold flops. Precisely, work over $\mathbb C$ with the Axiom of Choice in the complete-local isolated cDV smooth flopping setting. Fix its projective crepant resolution $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, with nonsingular source, nonempty exceptional union of curves, and an isomorphism away from the closed point. Form the generic ADE slice pair $(\Delta,J)$ from this chosen resolution, and use the setting's specified basic Van den Bergh bundle and NCCR. For the finite ADE Coxeter system on $\Delta$, the relative arrangement $(\operatorname{Cone}(J)^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$ identifies with the finite geometric flop arrangement, and its relative complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ identifies with that arrangement's complexified complement. Its chambers label minimal models and their corresponding NCCR derived categories. Adjacency means sharing a wall and corresponds to flop equivalences with the chamber dictionary's convention. Geodesics, meaning chamber paths of minimum length for their endpoints, give naturally isomorphic composites when their source and target agree. At a chosen chamber and basepoint, $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C})$ acts by derived autoequivalences modulo natural isomorphism.

Such intersection arrangements need not be Coxeter arrangements. The original article also reports Iyama--Wemyss low-rank classifications; that bibliographical report is attribution rather than a classification theorem supplied here.

rem-two-generator-root-characterisation-.title: Root characterization of the inverse two-generator element

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be the Coxeter system indexed by a set $\Gamma_0$, possibly infinite, with its standard geometric representation and positive and negative roots $\Phi^+$ and $\Phi^-$. For $L\subseteq\Gamma_0$, let $W_L$ be the subgroup generated by the simple generators indexed by $L$, let $\Phi_L$ be its associated parabolic root set, and put $\Phi_L^\pm=\Phi_L\cap\Phi^\pm$. An associate of $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ is a subset whose standard parabolic subgroup is conjugate to $W_J$.

Let $I$ be an associate of $J$, let distinct $a,b\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$ satisfy $|\Phi_{I\cup\{a,b\}}\setminus\Phi_I|<\infty$, and put $T=I\cup\{a,b\}$. Let $v_{a,b,I}$ be the two-generator element constructed in the proof of the minimal common left multiple lemma. Then $v_{a,b,I}^{-1}$ is the unique $w\in W_T$ satisfying $w(\Phi_T^+\setminus\Phi_I^+)\subseteq\Phi_T^-$ and $w(\Phi_I^+)\subseteq\Phi_T^+$.

rem-universal-cayley-graph-artin-tits-no.title: Universal wall graph as a groupoid Cayley graph

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, with simple generators $s_a$ indexed by $a\in\Gamma_0$, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Let $\Theta$ be the real dual reflection space, $\Theta_J=\{f\in\Theta:f(\alpha_j)=0\ (j\in J)\}$, and $(T_J,\mathcal H^J)=(\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ,\mathcal H^J)$ the relative arrangement, with interior taken in $\Theta_J$. Relative chambers are the connected components of $T_J\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}H$; walls and adjacency use chamber closures in $\Theta_J$ and the codimension-one wall convention. Identify these chambers with the algebraic labels $A=(x,I)\in\mathrm{Cham}(J)$. Write $\mathcal{BH}(J)$ for the Brink–Howlett groupoid, $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ for its universal wall groupoid, and $\mathcal F$ for the covering that sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and an arrow to its label. Composition is read from left to right.

Let $L$ be the set of tagged base arrows $\sigma=v_{a,I}:I\to K$ realized as images under $\mathcal F$ of adjacent wall crossings upstairs. The crossing element and its target subset depend only on $I,a$. Define two labelled directed graphs with the same label set $L$. The universal generating graph has vertex set $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ and arc set consisting of $(A,\sigma,B)$ whenever $A,B$ are adjacent and their unique upstairs arrow maps to $\sigma$. The right Cayley graph of $\mathcal{BH}(J)$ based at $J$ has vertices all tagged arrows $g:J\to I$, for all base objects $I$, and arcs $(g,\sigma,g\sigma)$ for every $\sigma:I\to K$ in $L$ and every such $g:J\to I$. A label-preserving directed graph isomorphism is a vertex bijection that preserves and reflects these labelled arc triples.

These graphs are isomorphic: the isomorphism sends $A$ to the image under $\mathcal F$ of the unique arrow $(1,J)\to A$.

When $J=\varnothing$, the relative arrangement is the Coxeter arrangement: $(T_\varnothing,\mathcal H^\varnothing)=(\mathrm{Cone}^\circ,\mathcal H)$. Moreover $\mathcal{BH}(\varnothing)$ has one object and arrow group $W$. The generating graph is the ordinary right Cayley graph of $W$ on the simple generators: its vertices are $x\in W$ and its arcs are $(x,s_a,xs_a)$. In particular $v_{a,\varnothing}=s_a$.

rem-universal-cover-existence-artin-tits.title: Existence of universal connected groupoid covers

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Every nonempty connected small groupoid $\mathcal G$ has a universal connected groupoid covering $F:\widetilde{\mathcal G}\to\mathcal G$. For every object $x$ of $\mathcal G$, the deck transformation group $\operatorname{Deck}(F)$ is isomorphic to the vertex group $\mathcal G_x$.

Here a groupoid is a category in which every morphism is invertible; connected means that any two objects are joined by a morphism. The vertex group at $x$ consists of the morphisms from $x$ to itself. A covering has a unique lift of each base morphism from each prescribed object over its source. It is universal when all upstairs vertex groups are trivial. A deck transformation is an automorphism of the upstairs groupoid whose composite with $F$ equals $F$.

rem-wall-notation-artin-tits-normalisers.title: Wall-crossing notation and Brink–Howlett convention

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Use the simple wall-crossing convention $v_{a,I}=w_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D$, where $D=[I,a]$ is the connected component containing $a$ in the diagram on $I\cup\{a\}$, $a\notin I$, and $W_D$ is finite.

The article's Remarks 3.18–3.19 say that $\omega_{a,I}$ may be abbreviated to $\omega_a$ when the source is clear, following its reference [24, Definition 1.28], and report that $v_{a,I}$ is the inverse of the element denoted $v[a,I]$ by Brink–Howlett, whose Section 2 also treats $v[I,J]$ for certain disjoint subsets. This sentence records the original authors' attribution; the 1999 original has not been read here.

Independently, the general Coxeter-system convention of Dyer–Gimenez gives
$$\nu(a,I)=w_Dw_{D\setminus\{a\}}=v_{a,I}^{-1}.$$
Thus the inverse product comparison holds whenever the connected support $D$ is spherical, without assuming that $W$, $W_I$, or $W_{I\cup\{a\}}$ is finite. This verified comparison uses Dyer–Gimenez's symbol $\nu(a,I)$; it does not claim direct verification of the historical symbol $v[a,I]$.

rem-wall-root-characterisation-artin-tit.title: The printed root characterization of a wall-crossing element

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system indexed by the vertex set $\Gamma_0$. For $L\subseteq\Gamma_0$, let $W_L$ be the subgroup generated by the simple reflections indexed by $L$, let $\Phi_L$ be its associated root set, and put $\Phi_L^{\pm}=\Phi_L\cap\Phi^{\pm}$. thm-artin-normaliser-splitting-artin-tit.title: Spherical Artin normaliser splitting

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, and let $J$ be a subset of its vertex set. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $A_J$ its standard parabolic subgroup. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid, and write $\mathcal R_J$ for its vertex group at $J$, consisting of its arrows from $J$ to $J$ under composition.

The normaliser $\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ is the internal semidirect product $A_J\rtimes\mathcal R_J$: each normaliser element has a unique expression $pr$ with $p\in A_J$ and $r\in\mathcal R_J$. Consequently the quotient homomorphism restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$, where $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$.

thm-atomic-matsumoto-artin-tits-normalis.title: Atomic Matsumoto theorem

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with diagram vertex set $\Gamma_0$, with no restriction on its rank or type, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. An associate of $J$ is a subset whose standard parabolic subgroup is conjugate to $W_J$. The Brink–Howlett groupoid $\mathcal{BH}(J)$ has these associates as objects; a morphism $w:I\to K$ is an element of $W$ carrying the simple roots indexed by $K$ onto those indexed by $I$, and composable labels multiply from left to right. A standard expression is a finite composable sequence of elementary wall-crossing morphisms whose Coxeter lengths sum to the length of their product. An atomic braid relation replaces one of the two standard expressions for a two-generator common prefix by the other, under the finite relative-root hypothesis of the atomic braid definition.

For associates $I,K$ of $J$ and $w\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{BH}(J)}(I,K)$, any two standard expressions of $w$ are related by a finite sequence of atomic braid relations.

thm-finite-simplicial-asphericity-artin-.title: Deligne asphericity used for the relative complement

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let $\mathcal H$ be a finite collection of linear hyperplanes. Suppose every chamber, meaning every connected component of $V\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}H$, is an open simplicial cone: it is the image of an open positive orthant under a linear isomorphism onto $V$. Write $V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, with complex scalar multiplication $z\cdot(v\otimes w)=v\otimes zw$ and its finite-dimensional Euclidean topology. Then the complexified complement $M=V_{\mathbb C}\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$ is nonempty and path-connected, admits a CW structure, and has vanishing homotopy groups in all degrees at least two. Choose a vertex $b$ of such a CW structure and put $\pi=\pi_1(M,b)$. With the identity identification of this fundamental group with $\pi$, the based space $(M,b)$ is a $K(\pi,1)$. Here a $K(\pi,1)$ means a connected based CW complex with a specified fundamental-group isomorphism to $\pi$ and vanishing higher homotopy groups; the latter vanishing is called asphericity.

In particular, let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with $W$ finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. For its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$ and relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$, the space $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ admits a CW structure and, after choosing a vertex basepoint, is a $K(\pi,1)$ for its own fundamental group with the identity identification.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let $\mathcal H$ be a finite collection of linear hyperplanes. Suppose every chamber, meaning every connected component of $V\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}H$, is an open simplicial cone: it is the image of an open positive orthant under a linear isomorphism onto $V$. Write $V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, with complex scalar multiplication $z\cdot(v\otimes w)=v\otimes zw$ and its finite-dimensional Euclidean topology. Then the complexified complement $M=V_{\mathbb C}\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$ is nonempty and path-connected, admits a CW structure, and has vanishing homotopy groups in all degrees at least two. Choose a vertex $b$ of such a CW structure and put $\pi=\pi_1(M,b)$. With the identity identification of this fundamental group with $\pi$, the based space $(M,b)$ is a $K(\pi,1)$. Here a $K(\pi,1)$ means a connected based CW complex with a specified fundamental-group isomorphism to $\pi$ and vanishing higher homotopy groups; the latter vanishing is called asphericity.

In particular, let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with $W$ finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. For its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$ and relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$, the space $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ admits a CW structure and, after choosing a vertex basepoint, is a $K(\pi,1)$ for its own fundamental group with the identity identification.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, with canonical real reflection representation, dual action and Tits cone $U$, and fix $J\subseteq S$. For $I\subseteq S$, write $W_I=\langle I\rangle$, put $E_I=\{f:f(\alpha_i)=0\ (i\in I)\}$, and let $C_I$ consist of the vectors in $E_I$ positive on the simple roots indexed by $S\setminus I$. Set $E=E_J$, with its Euclidean topology, $T=U\cap E$ and $T^\circ=\operatorname{int}_E T$. A $J$-chamber label is a pair $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ such that $x$ has minimum Coxeter length in $xW_I$; it labels the $J$-chamber $xC_I$ in the relative-interior arrangement. For a root $\alpha$ put $H_\alpha=\{f:f(\alpha)=0\}$. The arrangement hyperplanes are the proper traces $E\cap H_\alpha$ meeting $T^\circ$. A wall is a nonempty intersection of a chamber's closure in $E$ with an arrangement hyperplane, of affine dimension $\dim E-1$.

Let $(x,I)$ be a $J$-chamber label, let $a\in S\setminus I$, and put $K=I\cup\{a\}$. Suppose $W_K$ is finite. For a finite standard parabolic $W_L$, write $w_L$ for its longest element and $\iota_L$ for the permutation of $L$ determined by $w_L\alpha_s=-\alpha_{\iota_L(s)}$. Define $b=\iota_K(a)$ and $(y,I')=(xw_Iw_K,K\setminus\{b\})$. Then $(y,I')$ is a $J$-chamber label, its chamber is adjacent to $xC_I$ through the common wall $\overline{xC_K}$, and crossing back at $b$ returns $(x,I)$. Here the bar denotes closure in $E$, and $xC_K$ is the relative interior of that wall in its affine hull.

Call $J$ strongly Dynkin if $J$ is a proper subset of $S$ and $W_{J\cup\{s\}}$ is finite for every $s\in S\setminus J$. If $J$ is strongly Dynkin, any two $J$-chamber labels are connected by a finite sequence of the crossings just described.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: A covering $p:(E,e)\to(G,x)$ of nonempty connected small groupoids is a functor bijective on arrows with every fixed source. It is determined up to unique pointed isomorphism over $G$ by its characteristic subgroup $H=p(E_e)\le G_x$; unpointed isomorphism classes correspond to conjugacy classes of subgroups of $G_x$. A normal covering means that its deck transformations act transitively on one, hence every, fibre. This is equivalent to $H\lhd G_x$, and then $G_x/H\cong\mathrm{Deck}(p)$. Here arrow products are left to right and deck transformations use ordinary function composition; the isomorphism sends $aH$ to the deck transformation sending $e$ to the endpoint of the lift of $a$. Every such $G$ has a universal connected covering with trivial vertex groups, obtained by taking $H=\{1_x\}$.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $S$ is finite and $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ its standard projection, and $P=\ker\pi$. For $G=W,A$, let $G_J$ be the subgroup generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$, and define $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $\Theta_J$ be the subspace of the real dual reflection representation on which the simple roots indexed by $J$ vanish, and let $\mathcal H^J$ consist of the distinct hyperplanes obtained by restricting to $\Theta_J$ those root hyperplanes that do not contain it. In spherical type, the relative complexified complement is $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}=(\Theta_J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$, with its subspace topology. The action of $N(W,J)$ on $X$ is the complex-linear extension of $(nW_J)\cdot f=nf$, where $(nf)(v)=f(n^{-1}v)$ for $f\in\Theta_J$, $v$ in the real root space and $n\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$. It is independent of the representative and preserves $X$. For $x\in X$, let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$ under this action.

The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\to N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Moreover, $X$ is a $K(N(P,J),1)$ and $X/N(W,J)$ is a $K(N(A,J),1)$: here $K(G,1)$ means a path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to $G$ and whose homotopy groups in all degrees at least two vanish. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, let $\pi:A\to W$ be its standard projection and let $P=\ker\pi$. Write $W_J$ and $A_J$ for the subgroups generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$. For $G=W,A$, put $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified hyperplane complement, let $x\in X$, and let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$. The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and $\overline C$ a closed convex polyhedral cone with nonempty interior $C$. A wall is the hyperplane spanned by a codimension-one face of $\overline C$. For each wall choose a linear reflection fixing it, meaning a linear transformation of order two whose fixed space is that wall. Let $S$ be the set of these reflections and let $W$ be the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(E)$ generated by $S$. Assume $wC\cap C=\varnothing$ for every nonidentity $w\in W$; this is a Vinberg system.

Put $T=\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C)$ and let $\mathcal A$ be the set of fixed hyperplanes of all reflections in $W$. Then $T$ is a nonempty open convex cone, $\mathcal A$ is a locally finite arrangement in $T$, and $W$ preserves both. Give $M=(T\times T)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal A}(H\times H)$ the subspace topology and let $W$ act diagonally. This action is free and properly discontinuous and is a covering-space action. The space $M$ is path connected, and $M\to M/W$ is a regular covering with deck group $W$.

The pair $(W,S)$ is a Coxeter system. For distinct $s,t\in S$, let $m(s,t)$ be the order of $st$, possibly infinite. Let $A$ be the group generated by $\sigma_s$ for $s\in S$, with the relation equating the two alternating words of length $m(s,t)$ beginning respectively with $\sigma_s$ and $\sigma_t$ whenever $m(s,t)$ is finite. Let $\theta:A\to W$ send $\sigma_s$ to $s$, and put $P=\ker\theta$. For a basepoint $z\in M$ and its image $\bar z\in M/W$, the covering sequence $1\to\pi_1(M,z)\to\pi_1(M/W,\bar z)\to W\to1$ is isomorphic, as a sequence over $W$, to $1\to P\to A\xrightarrow{\theta}W\to1$. Here $\pi_1$ is the group of based loop homotopy classes, and the map to $W$ records the endpoint translate of a lifted loop.

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system in its canonical real representation $V=\mathbb R^S$, with basis $(\alpha_s)$, dual $\Theta$, root system $\Phi$, contragredient action, and Tits cone $U$. For $I\subseteq S$ put $E_I=\{f:f(\alpha_i)=0\ (i\in I)\}$ and $C_I=\{f\in E_I:f(\alpha_s)>0\ (s\notin I)\}$. Fix $J\subseteq S$ and put $E=E_J$, $T=U\cap E$, and $T^\circ=\operatorname{int}_E T$. Let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ and let $\ell$ denote Coxeter length. The pairs $(x,I)$, with $x\in W$ and $I\subseteq S$, satisfying $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $\ell(x)=\min\{\ell(y):y\in xW_I\}$ label the $J$-chambers bijectively by $(x,I)\mapsto xC_I$. These are exactly the chambers of $(T^\circ,\mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A=\{E\cap H_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi,\ E\not\subseteq H_\alpha\}$, with traces missing $T^\circ$ omitted. No sphericity assumption on $J$ is imposed.

thm-salvetti-topology-input-artin-tits-p.title: Independent Salvetti homotopy-model input

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $I$ be a nonempty open convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space $E$ and $\mathcal A$ a locally finite arrangement of linear hyperplanes meeting $I$. Let $M(I,\mathcal A)$ be the product complement of *Complexified complements in an open convex cone*, and let $\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)$ be the simplicial CW model of *The Salvetti order complex and its finite CW case*.

There exists a homotopy equivalence $f:\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)\to M(I,\mathcal A)$, with homotopy equivalence understood as in *Homotopy equivalences, homotopy inverses and spaces of the same homotopy type*. If $\mathcal A$ is finite, the model is finite; in particular this holds for a finite arrangement in the whole vector space.

For the additional equivariant assertion, let $(W,S)$ be a Vinberg system in $E$ with closed fundamental chamber $\overline C$, in the sense specified in *Independent Artin fundamental-group identification*. Require $I=\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C)$ and $\mathcal A=\{\operatorname{Fix}(r):r\in W\text{ is a linear reflection}\}$, the Coxeter arrangement of this realization. For the actions of *Linear symmetries act on the Salvetti model*, $f$ can be chosen $W$-equivariant: $f(wx)=wf(x)$ for every $w\in W$ and $x\in\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)$, as in *Equivariant maps and isomorphisms of group actions*.

Under these additional Vinberg hypotheses, for each of $X=\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)$ and $X=M(I,\mathcal A)$, let $X/W$ be the set of orbits for the relation $x\sim y$ if $y=wx$ for some $w\in W$. Give it the quotient topology: $U\subseteq X/W$ is open exactly when $q_X^{-1}(U)$ is open in $X$, where $q_X(x)=[x]$. With these topologies, the induced map $\overline f:\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)/W\to M(I,\mathcal A)/W$, $\overline f([x])=[f(x)]$, is a homotopy equivalence.

If I is the open Tits cone of a Vinberg realization (W,S) and A is its Coxeter arrangement, f can be chosen W-equivariant, and its induced map Sal(A)/W→M(A)/W is a homotopy equivalence.

Require $I=\operatorname{int}(\bigcup_{w\in W}w\overline C)$ and $\mathcal A=\{\operatorname{Fix}(r):r\in W\text{ is a linear reflection}\}$, the Coxeter arrangement of this realization. For the actions of *Linear symmetries act on the Salvetti model*, $f$ can be chosen $W$-equivariant: $f(wx)=wf(x)$ for every $w\in W$ and $x\in\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)$, as in *Equivariant maps and isomorphisms of group actions*.

Under these additional Vinberg hypotheses, for each of $X=\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)$ and $X=M(I,\mathcal A)$, let $X/W$ be the set of orbits for the relation $x\sim y$ if $y=wx$ for some $w\in W$. Give it the quotient topology: $U\subseteq X/W$ is open exactly when $q_X^{-1}(U)$ is open in $X$, where $q_X(x)=[x]$. With these topologies, the induced map $\overline f:\operatorname{Sal}(I,\mathcal A)/W\to M(I,\mathcal A)/W$, $\overline f([x])=[f(x)]$, is a homotopy equivalence.

thm-spherical-artin-garside-input-artin-.title: Independent spherical Artin Garside input

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
For a spherical Artin system, its positive Artin monoid embeds in its Artin group as a Garside monoid. Its simples are the positive lifts of elements of the Coxeter group. Gcds and lcms exist on both sides.

More explicitly, spherical means that the Coxeter group $W$ is finite. The positive monoid $M$ and the Artin group $A$ are given by the same standard braid presentation in the monoid and group categories. Let $w_0$ be the longest element of $W$ and $\Delta=\boldsymbol{w_0}$ its reduced-word lift in $M$. The canonical map identifies $M$ with the positive submonoid $A^+\subseteq A$ and transports the Garside structure with Garside element $\sigma_{w_0}$. In the categorical convention $x\Delta=\Delta\phi(x)$, simples are the left divisors of $\Delta$; they are also precisely its right divisors, and are exactly $\{\boldsymbol w:w\in W\}$. In $A^+$ these are $\{\sigma_w:w\in W\}$.

Definition 2.1 supplies cancellation, noetherianity, both divisibility lattices and simple atoms; Definition 2.5 defines simple elements as left divisors of Delta.

thm-spherical-deligne-topology-artin-tit.title: Spherical relative arrangements and Deligne topology

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, let $J\subseteq S$, and use its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative cone $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$, positive arrangement category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ and groupoid completion $\mathcal D(J)$. Suppose $W$ is finite, also called spherical type. Then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ=\Theta_J$, and $(\Theta_J,\mathcal H^J)$ is a finite central simplicial arrangement: its hyperplanes are finite in number, pass through the origin, and each chamber is a linear image of an open positive orthant in $\Theta_J$.

The category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ has a finite-type atomic categorical Garside structure. Thus its completion $\mathcal D(J)$ is a Garside groupoid in the sense of being the groupoid completion of that Garside category. It is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C})$ of the relative complexified complement. These deductions use the finite simplicial hypotheses; no extension to a general nonsimplicial or infinite arrangement is asserted.

thm-universal-brink-howlett-cover-artin-.title: Universal Brink–Howlett covering and its deck group

statement.heading: Statement
statement.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of arbitrary rank in its standard real root representation, with diagram vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and fix arbitrary $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Put $W_I=\langle s_i:i\in I\rangle$ and $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. Let $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ be the algebraic label set of pairs $(x,I)$ with $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ of minimum length in $xW_I$. Write $\mathcal{BH}=\mathcal{BH}(J)$ for the Brink–Howlett groupoid and $\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}=\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}(J)$ for the groupoid with these labels as objects and one arrow $(x,I)\to(y,K)$ labelled $x^{-1}y$. The functor $\mathcal F:\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}\to\mathcal{BH}$ defined by $(x,I)\mapsto I$ and $x^{-1}y\mapsto x^{-1}y$ is a universal groupoid covering, with $\operatorname{Deck}(\mathcal F)\cong N(W,J)$ and $\mathcal{BH}\cong\widetilde{\mathcal{BH}}/N(W,J)$.

For the geometric interpretation, use the finite-rank relative-cone convention: the set $\Gamma_0$ is finite, while neither $W$ nor $W_J$ is required to be finite and $J$ is arbitrary. Then the objects upstairs are exactly the relative chambers, and the adjacent-wall arrows map to the Brink–Howlett generators $v_{a,I}:I\to K$. Here $I$ is an associate of $J$, $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, $D=[I,a]$ is the component containing $a$ in the diagram induced on $I\cup\{a\}$, and $W_D$ is finite. The family is given by $v_{a,I}=w_{D\setminus\{a\}}w_D$ and $K=(I\cup\{a\})\setminus\{\iota_D(a)\}$, where $w_L$ is the longest element of a finite standard parabolic $W_L$ and $w_D\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_D(i)}$ defines $\iota_D$. The projected adjacent crossings generate $\mathcal{BH}$.

article_section_3_5.locator: §3.5, PDF p.14: construction and finite simplicial specialization
article_section_3_5.raw_quote:
3.5. The Deligne groupoid. The Deligne groupoid was introduced in [9] to study the topology
of finite simplicial arrangements (and prove the K(π, 1) conjecture for finite real reflection groups).
Although our setting is more general than that of Deligne, the construction of the Deligne groupoid
can be carried out similarly. However, the key features proven by Deligne, namely that the Deligne
groupoid is a Garside groupoid equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the complexified com-
plement, only hold (to our knowledge) in the setting of finite simplicial arrangements.
  To the locally-finite arrangement (Cone(J)◦, HJ), we associate an oriented graph on the set
of vertices Cham(J). To every pair of adjacent chambers we associate a 2-cycle, i.e. given two
adjacent chambers (x, I) and (y, K) there is one arrow (x, I) →(y, K) and another opposite arrow
(y, K) →(x, I). We continue to use the notation ωa,I as above to label these arrows.
 A path in this graph from (x, I) to (y, K) is a geodesic if it is a path of minimal length between
(x, I) and (y, K). Equivalently, it crosses every hyperplane H ∈HJ at most once.
  Define D+ := D+(J) as the category with:
     • objects given by Cham(J); and
     • morphisms HomD+((x, I), (y, K)) are paths from (x, I) to (y, K) modulo the relation gen-
       erated by the identification of any two geodesic paths with the same source and target.
The arrangement groupoid D := D(J) associated to (Cone(J)◦, HJ) is defined as the groupoid
completion of D+.  If Γ is of spherical-type, then (Cone(J)◦, HJ) = (ΘJ, HJ) is a finite simplicial
arrangement, and we call D the Deligne groupoid. In this case, D is equivalent to the fundamental
            C             C
groupoid of XJ , denoted π1(X J ) [9].

carries a free and properly discontinuous action of W, and the quotient X C →X C/W is a normal
